    89→## ACCURACY AND PRECISION: LIMITS TO FORECASTING
    90→
    91→An astrologer, or one who uses the study of astrology to make forecasts or even predictions, is not the same as a psychic or clairvoyant, despite often being lumped together by those who do not understand the difference. One uses objective means to make forecasts, while the other relies on subjective means. An astrologer is capable of providing probabilities for forecasts based on historical facts and frequencies of occurrence, while a psychic or clairvoyant is not. Both may at times make forecasts or predictions based on personal observations and experiences, but that is not the same as providing evidence-based studies supporting probabilities derived from past frequencies of repetitive patterns. An astrologer examines the relationship of the planets to one another. Planets are also analyzed according to their relationship to the equinoxes and solstices. The vernal and autumnal equinoxes mark the beginnings of the signs Aries and Libra (spring and autumn as measured by the Earth’s orbit around the Sun). The solstices are identified as 0° Cancer and 0º Capricorn, or the start of summer and winter, based on the Earth’s orbital cycle. These are the points by which seasons are measured, which is also how much of human activity is organized. When a planet—or the Sun, in the case of a geo centric perspective—crosses one of these points, it begins a “cardinal sign” (Aries, Cancer, Libra, or Capricorn) for approximately the next 30 degrees of spatial arc. In the case of the Sun, it will remain in that cardinal sign for approximately 30 days. The next 30 degrees represent the “fixed signs,” or in the case of the Sun, the middle of the season. The last 30 degrees represent the “mutable signs,” or in the case of the Sun, the change of the seasons. Each of these planets and signs has different dynamics. They relate to different themes and dif ferent aspects of human experience or nature. For instance, some planets, including the Sun and Mars, are “hot.” Hence, the signs they rule—Leo and Aries—are also “hot.” They are known as “fire signs.” Thus, when “fire signs” are activated, there is much energy on Earth, but tempers can also flare, which in turn can lead to conflicts and threats of war. This can also correlate with hotter-thannormal temperatures, which may lead to droughts and famine. Now, a psychic might be able to claim to know which influence would dominate under a gathering of several planets in fire signs—war or droughts. But an astrologer, at best, might forecast one or the other, or perhaps state something like: “These placements can suggest the possibility of either a drought or war.” The astrologer cannot be certain exactly which type of event will unfold, but can suggest with confidence the themes involved and the types of events that may correlate with those themes. Furthermore, the astrologer can accurately identify “when” these themes and possible events are most likely to occur. A psychic or clairvoyant cannot consistently do this, although some may claim they can. Without astrology, their subjective vision of the future often lacks accuracy in predicting the timing of events. This brings up another difference between the two often-confused practices. An astrologer observes outer cosmic movements. It is an objective study in its own right. The interpretation of those movements may be subjective, but the timing is objective. This is not the case with psychics or clairvoyants, whose analysis is purely subjective, based on a “feeling” or “vision” they experience when in the presence of a client.
    92→
    93→<!-- PAGE 11 END -->
    94→
    95→In many cases, an astrological delineation of a chart may be misunderstood by those who think astrology, or the astrologer, “missed something” or was inaccurate because a specific event suggested did not happen. In other words, the narrower or more specific an astrologer’s inter pretation of a geocosmic signature, or even its timing, the more likely it will appear inaccurate. Astrology, in its purest interpretation, must allow for a wide range of possibilities to accurately reflect the meaning of a particular signature. This is important because the highest role of an astrologer is to help the client better understand the possibilities before them, so they (the client) can make informed choices in their life. The broader the communication of the themes and dynam ics involved, and the wider the timing of possible events under those themes and dynamics, the more accurate the astrologer will be. For instance, if an astrologer forecasted that between 2020 and 2025 the price of Bitcoin would be higher, that forecast would have been 100% accurate. But that is a very wide time band and would have missed the 80% price decline from November 2021 through November 2022. If that astrologer had said the price of Bitcoin would be higher every year between 2020 and 2025, the prediction would be inaccurate because of the collapse in 2022. The same would be true with stocks. One might say that stock indices will be higher every ten years. That is, if you invest in a stock market index at any time, the value of that index would be higher ten years later. That prediction is often used by salespeople of financial funds and would be correct—except after the high of 1929, when it took more than 20 years for stock markets to regain their value from the September 1929 peak. Is this type of prediction, with very broad and ten-year time bands, helpful? Perhaps it is for one who is very patient. Or would it be more helpful—and profitable—to know that during a certain year or period, the stock market has a high historical frequency of dropping at least 20%, or even 35% or more, according to histori cal evidence? An investor might be better off waiting for such a decline before investing in the stock market when it is making a new all-time high. There are arguments to support both sides of this question. However, the point is that there are limits to the degree of accuracy an astrologer can provide, especially when dealing with something as volatile as a financial market or a political trend. The best one can do is share the research—historical studies based on evidence that can yield prob abilities about the future, drawn from what has transpired in the past under the same or similar geocosmic signatures or cyclical time bands, especially when they overlap—and then make a projection of what that indicator suggests about the present or future. If the forecaster provides evidence of past correlations, and the market does not repeat this time as it did in the past, does that mean the astrologer or market timer was wrong? Or does that simply mean this was one of the fewer than 20% of instances in which a particular cycle didn’t happen as it had before? This is what an ethical astrologer can do: provide historical evidence and make a projection based on that evidence when the same indicators appear again. The examples above illustrate the limits of forecasting accuracy. The more specific the forecast is in terms of an event rather than a theme, the more likely the astrologer is to miss other dynamics that could unfold according to astrological principles. The more specific and narrower one is in forecasting a turn in a long-term market trend—a turn with a wide time band relative to the length of the cycle being examined— the more likely one is to miss it. A financial astrologer can, for instance, demonstrate that an 18-year U.S. stock market cycle has occurred 100% of the time within a 13- to 21-year interval since the market was founded in 1792. However, if the astrologer states unequivocally that it will happen in a specific year—say, 2026—that prediction has only a 12.5% chance of being exact (if
    96→
    97→<!-- PAGE 12 END -->
    98→
    99→given in 2021). In fact, every year in that 8-year time band has a 12.5% probability of being the exact year of the cycle. If one allows the entire time band to represent a possible 18-year cycle low, there is an excellent chance of being correct, as this has occurred in all cases so far. But as one tries to narrow that time band down to a single year, the odds of being correct begin to decline. How do we address those odds in an effort to narrow the time band down for such a long-term cycle’s culmination? We do this by overlapping smaller cycles, sub-cycles, or “phases” of the longer-term cycle. For example, an 18-year cycle might be composed of three 6-year sub-cycles or phases that have a normal range of 5-7 years. When the second phase is completed, we add 5-7 years to that date and see where it overlaps the 18-year cycle. For instance, if the last 18-year cycle in the U.S. stock market occurred in March 2009, then the odds are high that the next one will occur between 2022 and 2030. If we know that the last 6-year cycle ended in 2022, and in over 80% of historical cases this sub-cycle has occurred every 5-7 years, we can project that it is next due in 2028 +/– 1 year, overlapping the 18-year cycle time band. This is where the probabili ties, based on historical studies, are greatest. But the 6-year cycle is not 100% reliable—it is just over 80%. So, if the cycle low does not happen in 2028 +/– 1 year, but instead happens in, say, 2026 or 2030—still within the 100% historical time band for the 18-year cycle, are we wrong? Or is this simply a case of the event happening slightly outside the 80% window? This illustrates the limits of accuracy in forecasting. The broader the interpretation and timing, the more accurate it will be. However, the broader and wider the timing of the event, the less useful it becomes for the reader to benefit from—or profit by. Efforts to narrow the time band and accuracy of a possible event do not end with cycle over laps. This is what distinguishes MMA from most market analysts. We also use geocosmic cycles that correlate with historical events and market culminations. The basic rule is this: the longer the planetary cycle that is unfolding, the more likely it will coincide with the end of a long-term market trend and the beginning of a new one. Likewise, the closer a long-term market cycle is to being due, the more likely a long-term planetary cycle will also be in effect. Given that the Aries V ortex, for example, is in effect in 2025-2026, and that it is the rarest celestial configuration of our lifetime, there is reason to think the all-time highs (the crest of the 18-year cycle) may be happening now. The crest is due at any time, as is the 18-year cycle trough, which is expected sometime before 2030. And since 35-65% declines tend to occur after such a long-term bullish trend ends, what should the prediction be? More importantly, what should a stock market investor’s strategy be over the next couple of years? That question not only illustrates the limits of forecasting but also the value of applying these timing methods with an understanding of their odds and importance. If you can avoid buy ing when a market is making an all-time high and instead wait for a 37-63% decline that is due before entering, which offers a better possibility of long-term profits? This is why market timing, when used effectively, gives an investor better odds of success. You don’t have to be exact in your timing, but it is helpful to know the limits and probabilities. Knowledge of cycle studies combined with geocosmics provides this “edge.” It is an edge that all traders and investors seek.    107→## BRIEF NOTE TO INVESTORS AND TRADERS IN 2026
   108→
   109→This year’s note is directed more to investors than to traders. The reason is that an important longterm planetary cycle is in force: the 36-year Saturn–Neptune conjunction on February 20, 2026. Longterm planetary cycles most often correlate with the completion of long-term market cycles. Further more, predicting the exact turn of such cycles within a narrow time band is never easy when a long-term planetary cycle is unfolding. There are many possibilities within the orb of influence of such a cycle. The historical orb of influence for a long-term stock market cycle connected to the Saturn–Neptune conjunction is eleven months. The conjunction is exact on February 20, 2026, which means a long-term cycle crest or trough (or both) is due between March 2025 and February 2027. However, this can be narrowed down because, in all but one case, the range was eight months or less. This suggests the highest probability for a long-term cycle to end lies between June 2025 and October 2026. We may be able to reduce this further if we take into account that in July 2025, these two outer planets came within just 13′ of their exact conjunction. If that counts, then allowing an 8-month orb from that time yields a range of November 2024 to March 2026. The overlap of March 2025 to March 2026 would stand out as a potential long-term trend change. But it may expand to eight months beyond the exact conjunction in February 2026 as well. What type of long-term stock market cycle is due? As stated in The Ultimate Book on Stock Market Timing: Geocosmic Correlations to Investment Cycles: The Saturn–Neptune conjunction has a definite correlation to long-term cycle crests. In some cases, these cycles were 18-year crests, and in others, they were simply phases of the 18-year cycle. Investors may use this signature as an opportunity to take profits on long-term holdings if the market is rallying into it, for the probabilities are great that a 4-year cycle will top out within the central time band, or close by. The U.S. stock market is in the time band for its 18-year cycle crest and trough, which extends from 2025 through 2030 in the case of the trough, with the crest due before that. But it could also be in the time band for a 4-year cycle crest and trough, measured from the low of September 2022. In the case of a 4-year cycle, we would anticipate a decline from the high of at least 16%. In the case of an 18-year cycle crest, we would anticipate a decline of 35-65%. Since the 18-year cycle will be starting its 17th year from the low of 2009, and bull runs to the crest of the next 18-year cycle have historically lasted 9-20 years, one can see that it is getting very late for the 18-year cycle crest to be completed. With this in mind, our advice to investors is very simple: start looking for signs to scale back on long-term equity holdings or to hedge them in the event that a severe decline is approaching. You may also want to begin adjusting your portfolio with the idea that cash will soon be king again. But even that is a concern, because the Aries V ortex suggests that the Dollar may continue its decline relative to other currencies over the next three years. For this reason, investors are advised to consider diversifying their portfolios away from solely U.S. dollar-denominated assets and into those backed by other currencies, especially those of neutral countries, countries with economies heavily supported by commodities, and stable Asian currencies. Once the U.S. stock market declines 37-63%, consider moving back into U.S. equities.

   119→## TRANSITION OF LEADERSHIP UNDER THE ARIES VORTEX
   120→
   121→They say ev’ry man needs protection, They say ev’ry man must fall. Yet I swear I see my reflection Some place so high above this wall. I see my light come shining From the west unto the east. Any day now, any day now, I shall be released. —Bob Dylan, “I Shall Be Released,” Music from Big Pink (The Band, 1968) Worry and anxiety are only a matter of the time it takes us to adjust to the Truth. —Damien Simpson and Ray Merriman interview, Universal Mind Science, Hollywood, California, early 1980s I have never lived in a time when the U.S. was not the world’s dominant superpower. I have never lived in a world where the U.S. Dollar was not the dominant standard world currency. I have never lived during a period when the U.S. did not have strong allies throughout the world who trusted it to be the leader of world order and global security. However, that is all changing as we enter the midpoint of the “New Aira” of 2020– 2032, which just happens to coincide with the “Aries V ortex” of 2025–2026. What is this “New Aira”? What exactly constitutes an “Aries V ortex”? And what correlation do these two extremely rare cosmic developments have with great changes in the world order? Can anything be done to affect how these changes unfold? Let’s review the larger New Aira cycle first. On December 21, 2020, Jupiter and Saturn conjoined at 0° Aquarius. This synodic cycle occurs approximately every 20 years. For roughly 200 years, those conjunctions take place in signs of the same element, with slight distortions near the beginning and end of each 200-year interval, when the series crosses the boundaries between elements. Between 1802 and 2000, for example, the conjunctions occurred mostly in earth signs, except in 1821, when the cycle reverted briefly to late Aries, and in 1980–81, when it leaped forward to the air sign of Libra. In 2000, the conjunction of Jupiter and Saturn returned for one final occurrence in the earth sign of Capricorn. The air-sign era is now underway with the Jupiter–Saturn conjunction in Aquarius on December 21, 2020. From 2020 through 2199, eight of the next nine Jupiter–Saturn conjunctions will occur in air signs. The air element of this synodic cycle has not been dominant since the 13th century, or approximately 800 years ago. Thus, as coined by market analyst and astrologer Kat Powell, we are now entering the “New Aira” cycle of the “Great Chronocrator,” a term often used to refer to the Jupiter–Saturn cycle.

   125→Of greatest importance right now is the first 12 years of the New Aira, or 2020–2032. This is the interval of time that it will take Jupiter to return to 0° Aquarius, the point from which the New Aira began. These 12 years will unfold as a sub-cycle within a greater cycle. It will likely take that long for humankind to begin to fully understand the New Aira transformation it is undergoing. It will take that long before the application of these new understandings registers in a meaningful, transformative, and enduring way—one that elevates human consciousness and clarifies the direction of the human experience. Until then, we are still learning what it means and how to use this new knowledge wisely. We already have a glimpse of the New Aira that is emerging and how it might manifest over time. Aquarius rules innovation, particularly in technology. One of the major themes associated with Aquarius is revolution and renaissance. In the past several Forecast books, it was noted that this would be a period of technological renaissance—and indeed it is. Yet we do not know quite yet how it will ultimately affect life on this planet. We see incredible possibilities. But there are also fears that it may lead to an ominous, even destructive, outcome for humanity. Will we be able to harness the power of this technological renaissance and use it constructively to improve life as we know it? Or will world leaders and other bad actors harness it first to control or destroy those they perceive as enemies? Answers to these questions during this first 12-year sub-cycle of the 200-year New Aira should begin to emerge as we continue through this period of transition. Sub-cycles are also known as phases. Just as this 12-year period is a sub-cycle, or phase, of the greater 200-year New Aira cycle, so too does the 12-year sub-cycle divide into two 6-year halfcycles. And half-cycles can be very dramatic, for they represent turning points in the pendulum swing of the greater cycle. It so happens that the midpoint of this first 12-year phase coincides with another powerful celestial configuration known as the “Aries V ortex.” The course of human activity and leadership is shifting. The pendulum of world leadership is swinging from the West back to the East. America’s standing as the world’s leader is vulnerable to being replaced by leadership from the opposite hemisphere—to a degree never experienced before by most people alive today. Will this change actually take place? Or is this just a temporary threat to the status of the U.S. that will reverse shortly? Will its currency, the U.S. dollar, survive this threat as the de facto global currency used for most world trade? If so, how will the U.S. regain its economic leadership? If not, where will that lead the U.S. and other nations of the world? Who will emerge as the new leader? These are the questions—even the challenges—that the U.S. and the world face as we enter the midpoint of the first 12-year phase of the New Aira. These are the realities coming to light as we enter the Aries V ortex. Nothing is quite the same. The world in this New Aira is filled with danger and uncertainty—a classical representation of Saturn conjunct Neptune in Aries. Yet it also offers incredible opportunities. Where there is fear, there is also opportunity for those who are alert and able to act in accordance with the changes signified by these times. For investors, this is a time to consider broadening one’s perspective—and one’s portfolio—to include the rise of new world leadership and assets backed by the currencies of these emerging world powers. In fact, the currencies themselves may change significantly, shifting from paper fiat to something more representative of this New Aira that began with the Jupiter–Saturn conjunction at 0° Aquarius. This is a techno-renaissance—and its currency is digital. It’s only a matter of time before we all need to adjust.

   131→## FEAR AND THE RE-IMAGINATION OF HOPE FOR THE FUTURE
   132→
   133→Everybody knows the war is over Everybody knows the good guys lost Everybody knows the fight was fixed The poor stay poor, the rich get rich That’ s how it goes Everybody knows Everybody knows that the boat is leaking Everybody knows that the captain lied Everybody got this broken feeling Like their father or their dog just died Everybody knows, everybody knows That’ s how it goes Everybody knows —Leonard Cohen, “Everybody Knows,” I’m Your Man (1988) History is seasonal and winter is here. —Neil Howe, “The Fourth Turning is Here,” Simon and Schuster, 2023. Welcome to “Crazy Times 2026.” This is the time of the long-anticipated “Aries V ortex,” an extremely rare celestial configuration centered on—and linked to—the Saturn–Neptune conjunction in the very first degree of Aries. Aries itself is the very first of 12 signs and marks the beginning of the world cycle according to astrology, the world’s oldest discipline exploring the correlation between cycles in the cosmos and cycles in human activity. Why are these “Crazy Times”? Because Saturn and Neptune correspond to more terms used in abnormal psychology than any other two planets. They represent very opposite dynamics, such as fear and hope, guilt and forgiveness, delusions of grandeur and persecution, certainty and disillusionment, mania and depression, irrational exuberance and panic. And in the first degree of Aries, this setup indicates a monumental shift from the end of one long-term cycle (Pisces) to the beginning of a new one (Aries). That is, Neptune only crosses into Aries every 164 years. Saturn does the same approximately every 29 years. The two planets conjoin one another every 36 years. But how often do these two planets conjoin one another right at the end and beginning of the 12 signs? Our database only goes back to about 4000 BC, and there are no instances of this same cosmic feat during that time. Some astrologers have suggested that this cosmic configuration happened at some point between 4000 and 8000 BC, but I cannot confirm that. To understand why the Aries V ortex of 2025–2026 is akin to “crazy times,” consider two things: (1) what is happening today, and (2) the principles associated with Saturn and Neptune, combined with the classic principles of Aries versus Pisces, the beginning of the cycle of signs versus the end of that cycle. In this case, it is not just an ordinary cycle but a very, very long one—over 4000 years in duration, at least.

   137→We must also take into account that the other two outermost planets—Uranus and Pluto—are in a favorable trine aspect, with their midpoint also crossing back and forth over 0° Aries, the very point of the Saturn–Neptune conjunction. These may seem like “crazy times” because they are unfolding under a geocosmic configuration that humanity has never before seen or experienced. Cosmic patterns this rare will usher in global changes of great magnitude, and life may seem so different that it feels a bit “crazy.” As we consider what has transpired already during the “orb of influence,” which began in early 2025 (when Saturn and Neptune entered Aries, followed by Uranus entering Gemini, and shortly Pluto finally entering Aquarius in November 2024), it is apparent that vast transforma tions are underway across multiple sectors of human activity. Figuratively speaking, everything that is supposed to be up has turned down, and everything that would normally be expected to turn down has instead turned up. What was previously regarded as diplomacy in the pursuit of world peace and global order has instead become driven by coercion and land- or money-grab bing, with little regard for consent or fairness toward those affected. The belief that “might is right,” and therefore entitles one to dictate the course of civilization rather than cooperate toward win-win outcomes and mutual benefit, has become the “new normal” of global leadership. This reflects one of the many expressions of Saturn in Aries (“the bully”), which will remain largely in effect through April 13, 2028. On a more positive note, Saturn in Aries can also represent superhuman efforts to build sys tems and structures that stand the test of time. However, this process is unlikely to unfold without resistance and struggle. Hence, there is often a challenge to authority and dominance. And without mutual respect among all parties involved, this can lead to conflict, or even the threat of war, where those with the most “might” can claim superiority and the mantle of power. Yet it is not just Saturn in Aries that indicates the harsh challenges that many experience today, especially those who find it difficult to adjust to this new reality (Aries). It is also Neptune, the planet of ideals, altruism, and the search for beauty and truth. Those guiding life principles are also being challenged. Even those who hold such fundamental religious beliefs as salvation in an after life for virtuous deeds committed in this life may find their belief systems challenged. One example of this cosmic dichotomy between Saturn and Neptune is the very simple con flict between hope and fear. Neptune represents hope, or the wish for a “better life,” even a perfect life—which, of course, is an illusion that can never be fully manifested on this plane. Yet it is a concept that can be imagined and moderated to mean simply a “better life” than the one currently being lived. Everyone has Neptune in their chart. Everyone has hope for a better life, a better world. For many, this belief is what keeps them going. It is supported by practices such as prayer and meditation, which are among the activities associated with Neptune. And then there is Saturn, the opposite counterpart to Neptune, representing fear or the reality that life is not perfect and, in many cases, not even fair. Where Neptune is idealistic and guilty of wishful thinking, Saturn is realistic, skeptical, controlling, and guilty of ... well, just plain guilt, either personally, for failing to do or attain something, or projecting (blaming) that “failure” onto others. Saturn represents boundaries, laws, and rules—the very things that help structure society into orderly collective behavior when built wisely and according to a sensible, well-thought-out plan. If one violates these boundaries, there is usually a consequence, a punishment, that follows. Or at least, that’s the way it used to be before the influence of the Aries V ortex began. Now the

Everybody wants change (Aries), but nobody wants to sacrifice security or the hope for a better future. Everyone wants change to move in a direction that is clear, understandable, and easy to adjust, one that provides a sense of self-control and selfdetermination. This is the downside of Neptune when it struggles to work constructively with Saturn, who demands both a realistic goal and an organized plan to achieve it. Without that possibility or belief, Neptune’s existence is in danger of falling into a state of hopelessness. One is then tempted to give up, surrender, or seek solace in altered states of consciousness. Hence, the rise in mental illness and substance abuse to escape (Neptune) the fears generated by the uncertainty of reality (Saturn). Living in today’s world of epic change is not easy. That is why this period (2026 +/– one year) is dubbed “Crazy Times.” Yet if one looks at the possibilities of this “New Aira” starting to unfold, one can also train the mind to see new possibilities—extraordinary opportunities. Therefore, once Saturn passes by as the planet front-running Neptune, the principles of the latter planet will again become visible. That is the hope. That is, Saturn is the faster-moving planet and “blocks out” the light of Neptune while it approaches and comes into conjunction with Neptune. Yes, Saturn may still domi nate until it finally leaves Aries, the sign also occupied by Neptune, in April 2028. But Neptune’s influence grows as Saturn starts its withdrawal from Neptune’s cosmic head and heart. The virtu ous Neptunian principle of compassion and care for others begins to express itself again. And as Saturn moves from the dominancy of fire-sign Aries into the more comfort- and security-motivated sign of Taurus, a return to normalcy—a deportation of “Crazy Times” into something less crazy and more humane—is scheduled to commence.   1154→
  1155→The Dollar/Yen had an inside year in 2025. The high of the year occurred early in the year, on January 10 at 158.87, while the low of the year occurred on April 22, 2025, at 139.86. This was below the high of 2024 but above the low of 2024 as well. Throughout most of the year, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) allowed interest rates on Japanese government bonds (JGBs) to rise. This caused some weakness in the Dollar/Yen exchange rate, but with the election of Sanae Takaichi in 2025, markets are starting to price in a return to “Abenomics” policies. These economic policies centered on weakening the Japanese Yen in order to manage the country’s debt load. This creates a backdrop for potential strength in the Dollar/Yen in 2025, and it is supported by the long-term cycle situation as well. Last year’s Conclusion section stated, “The weight of the evidence of the Dollar/Yen being in a new 4.125-year cycle is very compelling. The biggest question for the Dollar/Yen now, given its lateness of the 16.5-year cycle, is whether it can go on to make new cycle and multi-decade highs. Given the geocosmic backdrop, our bias is that USD/JPY will retest the 164.00 +/- 2.00 zone and probably rally as high as 175.00–177.00. It cannot entirely be ruled out that a 16.5-year cycle crest forms in 2025 in this zone of 175.00–177.00, but this is not our bias. On the contrary, the geocosmics of 2025 suggest we’re only getting a preview, due to retrograde motions, of a more profound crisis to come in the Dollar/Yen in 2026. Eventually, we could see the Dollar/Yen rally as high as 220.00–225.00, but probably not in 2025. This may coincide with the greater long-term 16.5-year cycle.” While the Dollar/Yen did not rally up to the target of 175.00–177.00, it held firmly in the 139.00 +/– 2.00 zone, essentially completing a double bottom to the September 2024 low. This low occurred seven months later, and it is not uncommon to see retests of important long-term cycle bottoms 6–22 months later. It will also be a matter of whether the Bank of Japan reverts to a more accommodative monetary policy and stops allowing yields on JGBs to rise. There may be a final attempt at lowering yields with the new administration in power.
  1156→
  1157→## THE LONG-TERM CYCLES IN THE DOLLAR/YEN
  1158→
  1159→The longest cycle to watch in the Dollar/Yen is 16.5 years. The prior low was on October 31, 2011, at 75.55, and 2026 starts the 15th year of the cycle. This long-term cycle points to a low around August 2028 +/– 3.5 years, so a low is due at any time. But first, the crest for this long-term cycle must be confirmed. As it stands, the crest from July 2024 at 161.99 is holding, but there is still a possibility that USD/JPY can rally one final time before reversing lower. Historically, the 16.5-year cycle broke down into phases lasting 5.5 years, or 55–77 months. However, in this cycle, a two-phase pattern composed of two 8.25-year cycles appears to have taken hold. An 8.25-year cycle trough unfolded in March 2020, making 2026 the sixth year in the 8.25-year cycle. This cycle is calling for a low between 2027 and 2029, so in theory, USD/JPY could still hit a new cycle high this year before beginning a drop into an 8.25-year cycle low. This 8.25-year cycle crest would form together with the 16.5-year cycle crest.
  1160→
  1161→<!-- PAGE 143 END -->
  1162→
  1163→USD/JPY Cycles Start/Progress as of 1/1/26 Next Due 16.5-year October 2011, 15 years 2025–2031 8.25-year March 2020, 6 years 2027–2029 4.125-year September 2024, 2 years 2027–2029 22.5-month September 2024, 16 months April 2026–December 2026 There is, however, a slim chance that a 16.5-year cycle bottom occurred in April 2025 with the low at 139.86. This is not a very likely scenario, but it is a possible one, especially if the 16.5-year cycle broke down into a three-phase pattern with three 5.5-year cycles. The 5.5-year cycle has a range of 55–77 months, and from the October 2011 low, the June 2016 low was 56 months. If the secondary low of January 2021 is considered with respect to the initial March 2020 low, it occurred 55 months from June 2016. Finally, the April 2025 low would be 51 months from January 2021, which is a bit short for a 5.5-year cycle trough; however, with a potential 16.5-year cycle bottom looming, it is not uncommon for shorter cycles to contract. This scenario is not a high-probability one, but it exists nonetheless. It represents the most bullish scenario for USD/JPY , as 2026 could start the first year of a new 16.5-year cycle. The 8.25-year cycle is then broken down into two 4.125-year cycle phases. The first 4.125-year cycle low within the 8.25-year cycle occurred on September 16, 2024, at 139.56. Forecast 2025 stated, “It’ s now the final 4.125-year cycle phase within the greater 8.25-year cycle phase, and we’re in the second 8.25-year cycle phase within the greater 16.5-year cycle. Thus, we expect this 4.125year cycle crest to coincide with the 16.5-year cycle crest too. A rally as high as 175.00-177.00 cannot be ruled out in 2025. Our bias is for the 164.00 +/- 2.00 zone to be tested, and then, eventually, exceeded given the new 4.125-year cycle.” It did not rally up to 175.00–177.00 in 2025, but this upside objective remains on the table for 2026 and beyond. The year 2026 will mark only the second year in the second and final 4.125-year cycle. This cycle’s crest will coincide with the greater 8.25-year and 16.5-year cycle crests.
  1164→
  1165→## THE INTERMEDIATE-TERM CYCLES IN THE DOLLAR/YEN
  1166→
  1167→The 4.125-year cycle breaks down further into either two 22.5-month cycle phases or three 17-month cycle phases. The 22.5-month cycle represents not only a half-cycle phase of the 4.125year cycle, but also one of the three phases of the 5.5-year cycle. The 4.125-year cycle that bottomed in September 2024 broke down into a three-phase pattern of 17-month phases. Forecast 2025 stated, “The question now is whether this final 4.125-year cycle phase to the greater 8.25-year cycle will break down into two 22.5-month or three 17-month cycles. It is still too early to tell, but January 2025 will begin the 4th month in this new intermediate-term cycle. Since it’ s the first phase of a new 4.125year cycle, we anticipate it to be bullish and rally into June or July at least.” So far, the high of this first phase of the 4.125-year cycle occurred on January 10, 2025, at 158.87. Thus, my expectation is for new cycle highs to follow in 2026, although it is not yet certain what the phase breakdown of this cycle will be. January 2026 will start the 16th month from the September 2024 low, and so if there is going to be a 17-month cycle phase, then a crest could be anticipated in the first quarter of 2026 at the latest. A low would be expected no later than April or May 2026. However, if there are going to be two 22.5-month cycle phases, USD/JPY could easily rally into the back half of 2026. A 22.5-month cycle trough would be due by December 2026, though. Even so, the intermediate-term cycles point to more upside for USD/JPY throughout the majority of 2026.
  1168→
  1169→<!-- PAGE 144 END -->
  1170→
  1171→## GEOCOSMICS
  1172→
  1173→There are a plethora of geocosmic setups that continue to warn of problems for the Japanese Yen in 2026. In other words, the outlook favors significantly more upside in 2026 and beyond. In all likelihood, the crest will be very climactic. The geocosmics in play for 2026 point to a resurgence in inflationary pressures, and the setup is shaping up to be bullish for USD/JPY . It begins with the conjunction between Saturn and Neptune at zero degrees Aries on February 20, 2026. Throughout 2025, the loose conjunction between these two planets kept a lid on inflation. Still, as they begin to separate in 2026, the restrictive forces of Saturn may no longer serve to contain the inflationary nature of Neptune in a fire sign. Then there is a series of aspects in July and August that could prove pivotal for debt markets, which are directly connected to currency markets. It begins with the trine between Uranus and Pluto, an aspect that will remain in effect into 2028. The central time band begins on July 18, and then two days later, there is a trine between Jupiter and Neptune, and an opposition between Jupiter and Pluto (both on July 20). With Pluto involved here, debt markets must be considered, as Pluto rules debt. With Jupiter and Neptune involved, inflation must be considered, as they corule this monetary phenomenon. There is another exact hit of Uranus trine Pluto toward the end of 2026 as well, on November 26. Each of these exact trines should be considered “hot spots” for a potential intervention in either debt or currency markets, and the Bank of Japan is well known for doing this. Speaking of Japan’s central bank, these outer-planetary transits should be considered in terms of aspects to its natal chart. The central bank’s official website states that it was estab lished on October 10, 1882, but the birth time is not provided, so we can only analyze aspects. Forecast 2025 stated, “For 2025, there are a few key transits that could compound the Bank of Japan’ s woes. On the top of the list is Uranus ingressing into Gemini on July 7. This is because Uranus will move into orb of an opposition with the BOJ’ s natal Venus at 2 degrees Sagittarius. Granted, there won’t be an exact aspect, as Uranus only makes it to the first degree of Gemini before retrograding back into Taurus on November 7. But still, Uranus opposite Venus is a
  1174→
  1175→<!-- PAGE 145 END -->
  1176→
  1177→classical transit for currency collapse or monetary shocks. However, around the same time, Nep tune ingressing into Aries will form a trine to the BOJ’ s natal Venus. Thus, the combined forces of Uranus and Neptune will be influencing Venus at the same time. Neptune may counteract some of the shock associated with Uranus and provide an illusion that all is under control, or it may lead to hysteria surrounding the collapse of the Japanese Yen. Keep in mind that it’ s in the first phase of a long-term cycle, which is usually when a market is at its most bullish. It’ s unlikely the crest of the 4.125-year cycle will occur in 2025, but rather, when the exact aspects to Venus take place in 2026.” Uranus makes its definitive ingress into Gemini on April 25, and by late June, there will finally be an exact opposition to the Bank of Japan’s natal Venus. Thus, I am looking for an acceleration to the upside in the value of the Dollar against the Yen throughout the summer of 2026. It is also worth noting that before this final ingress into Gemini takes place, Uranus will be conjunct the natal Pluto of the Bank of Japan. The central bank allowed interest rates on Japanese government bonds to rise throughout much of 2025, and this led to some strength in the Japanese Yen and weakness in the Dollar/Yen exchange rate. However, this policy is likely to be abandoned once Uranus moves away from Pluto in late Taurus. This would be consistent with a return to Abenomics-style policies in Japan, which are centered around weakness in the Japanese Yen and, therefore, a higher USD/JPY exchange rate. There are other transits to consider in the BOJ’s natal chart. Pluto forms an exact square with the Bank of Japan’s natal Mars in Scorpio starting in June–July of 2026. Although Mars rules Scorpio, Mars square Pluto is a classic signature of conflict. Pluto rules debt and manipulations. Forecast 2025 stated, “The Bank of Japan may literally be fighting (Mars) to keep their bonds (Pluto) from crashing, but in doing so, may lose complete control over the Yen’ s value. It’ s unlikely that this conflict will culminate in 2025, but by the end of the year, it will become very obvious that it’ s a serious issue.” As of this writing, the Dollar/Yen has not reached this crisis point, but the exact square between Pluto and Mars still has not occurred. There are stronger odds of this happening in 2026 compared with 2025.
  1178→
  1179→## CONCLUSION
  1180→
  1181→2026 will start only the second year in the second and final 4.125-year cycle phase within the greater 8.25-year cycle. The Dollar/Yen is in the second and final 8.25-year cycle phase within the greater 16.5-year cycle, of which 2026 starts the 15th year. Thus, the Dollar/Yen is in the late stages of multiple long-term cycles, but final phases can go parabolic and take markets to unthink able highs. The geocosmic backdrop is present in 2026 for a meteoric rise in the Dollar/Yen to occur, between Uranus’s opposition to the Bank of Japan’s Venus and Pluto’s square to the Bank of Japan’s Mars. My bias is that USD/JPY will retest the 164.00 +/– 2.00 zone early on in 2026 and, in all likeli hood, rally as high as 175.00–177.00 at some point during the year. If it cannot test, and preferably exceed, the 164.00 +/– 2.00 zone by June, it may be the case that the 16.5-year cycle already formed its crest back in 2024, although this is not my preferred outlook. In fact, given the geocosmic back drop in the coming years, I could see the Dollar/Yen surge as high as 220.00–225.00, but probably not in 2026. This would likely coincide with the greater long-term 16.5-year cycle.
  1182→
  1183→<!-- PAGE 146 END -->
  1184→
  1185→The most important cycle to watch for in terms of a crest and a reversal back lower in the Dollar/ Yen in 2026 is the 17-month or 22.5-month cycle. It is still unclear whether the 4.125-year cycle is breaking down into a two- or three-phase pattern. A 17-month cycle bottom is most likely by the first quarter of 2026, and it is likely to hold above 150.00–152.00. If this level were to break, it would increase the odds that the longer-term cycles are topping out. A break below 140.00–142.00 in 2026 would confirm that the 16.5-year cycle crest has peaked and that the Dollar/Yen could drop as low as 128.00–130.00, but this is not in my preferred playbook for 2026, especially given the signatures in the Bank of Japan’s chart and the inflationary mundane backdrop. Overall, 2026 appears to be a very bullish year for the Dollar/Yen as all of the factors are weighed.

  1189→## THE EURO
  1190→
  1191→by Ulric Aspegren, MMA Analyst
  1192→
  1193→## REVIEW
  1194→
  1195→In mid-November 2024, when the Euro report for the upcoming Forecast 2026 book was completed, the Euro was in freefall. The prices had managed previously to establish a peak at 1.127 USD in July 2023 (E), after rising 18% from an important trough at 0.953 USD in September 2022 (5). The prices tried to surpass this July 2023 crest, but stalled at 1.121 in September 2024, just below the tip of a massive triangle pattern. The situation did not look promising for the Euro, as it had already declined 5% from its September 2024 top. At the time, we were in the 25th month since the September 2022 bottom, and the question was: will the bearish trend endure, or is there hope for the bulls? Last year’s forecast detailed that the ongoing descent was a normal bullish correction to a 24-month cycle low, which was due to unfold sometime between April 2024 and March 2025. The prices kept falling, but finally reversed in the 28th month, on February 3, 2025, at 1.014 (6). A 24-month cycle trough was thus cemented within the time target, following an overall 10% decline from the 24-month cycle crest in July 2023 (E). As forecasted, the prices have since been in a bullish trend, rallying 17.5% so far to 1.1918 as of September 25, 2025. However, is this rally a sustainable affair, or is it just a transitory push-up from an intermediate-term cycle low before the Euro heads south again? The Euro closed on November 14, 2025, at 1.162.

  1201→## THE LONG-TERM CYCLES IN THE EURO
  1202→
  1203→My favored view is that a Euro greater cycle trough took place on September 28, 2022, at 0.954 USD (5). The prior greater cycle started in October 2000 (1) and was active for close to 22 years. We only have one previous greater cycle to compare with, which began in February 1985. It was opera tional for 16 years, as it ended in October 2000. Hence, it is possible that the greater cycle is a 19-year cycle, with a 3-year orb. However, my bias is that it is a 16-year cycle and that the previous 22-year cycle was a distorted greater cycle and thus an outlier. Time will have to tell. Assuming the 16-year cycle is the greater cycle, it should normally divide into two 8.4-year cycles. In its turn, the 8.4-year cycle has always split into two 4-year cycles. Hence, the assumed greater 16-year cycle should now be in its third year and a few months, off the September 2022 trough (5). This is the same for the 8.4-year and the 4-year cycles, as all three long-term cycles began at the same low (5). The current 4-year cycle is forecast to top out sometime between August 2025 and November 2026, at 1.313–1.584, an increase of 38%–66%. Once the prices have peaked out, they should head
  1204→

  1206→

  1208→
  1209→## THE 24-MONTH INTERMEDIATE-TERM CYCLE IN THE EURO
  1210→
  1211→My preferred outlook is that the 4-year cycle is separating into two 24-month intermediate-term cycles. Last year’s report stated: “We should thus be twenty-five months into this first intermediateterm cycle that began at the September 2022 low. As it is getting late in the cycle to make a higher high, my favored view is that the 24-month cycle crest was already established in July 2023 at 1.127 USD. If this is correct, then the Euro is on its way towards a 24-month cycle bottom, estimated to occur with its 6-month orb, sometime between April 2024 and March 2025.” Moreover, “The historical 6–20% bullish declines of the 24-month cycles generate a price target span of 0.897–1.056. The 38.2–61.8% retracement from the 1.127 crest to the 0.953 low produces a price objective range of 1.019–1.061. The overlap creates 1.019–1.056, as the most probable price target range for the forthcoming 24-month cycle low.” The 24-month cycle low was established on February 3, 2025, at 1.014 (6). This bottom occurred after an acceptable twenty-eight months from the September 2022 low and was within the set time target. The bottom was also within the historical price target span, but manifested slightly below the 61.8% retracement price level. Further, last year’s report stated: “Once the 24-month cycle low is in place, the prices are expected to rise within this second and current 24-month cycle to the 4-year cycle crest. This crest, already forecasted earlier, is anticipated to unfold sometime between August 2025 and November 2026, at 1.313–1.584 USD.” As the prices within this second 24-month cycle have overtaken the previous 24-month cycle crest of July 2023, at 1.127 (E), it confirms that the current 24-month cycle is in a bullish trend. The forthcoming 24-month cycle crest is anticipated to manifest sometime between March and November 2026, at 1.199–1.471 (an increase of 18–45%). When we overlap the objectives of the 4-year and the 24-month cycle crests, we obtain March–November 2026 and 1.313–1.471 as the most probable time and price targets for the 4-year cycle peak.
  1212→

  1214→
  1215→So far, the Euro has risen 17.5% from the February 3, 2025, low (6), establishing a yearly high on September 17, 2025 at 1.1918. We actually have to go back to the end of June 2021 to reach a higher price level. Once the 4-year cycle crest is in place, the prices are expected to decline to the 4-year cycle trough, projected to take place sometime between December 2025 and October 2027. We can narrow down this time target range with the time objective for the second 24-month cycle low, estimated to occur with its 6-month orb, in the time frame August 2026–August 2027. The 4-year cycle low should manifest at historical price declines of 14.8–25.8%. You may overlap this range with the 38.2–61.8% retracement from the newly formed 4-year cycle crest to the 0.953 low of September 2022 (5), to obtain the most probable price target span for the 4-year cycle bottom.
  1216→
  1217→## GEOCOSMICS
  1218→
  1219→The current 4-year cycle is expected to peak out sometime in the concentrated time band of March–November 2026. We have the important Saturn–Neptune conjunction in February 2026. As this planetary pair connects only once, we will extend the timing by four months on either side of the conjunction, which generates a time period of October 2025–June 2026. Via overlapping, we acquire March–June 2026, which is the most probable timing for the 4-year cycle crest. As already seen, the 4-year cycle low is then expected to cement, at the latest, by August 2027.
  1220→
  1221→## TECHNICALS
  1222→
  1223→As you can see on the chart, the prices have managed since last year’s report to surpass a sub stantial resistance line, which joins the 2001 and the 2017 lows. As long as prices can stay above this now important support line, the bulls are in control. If we look to the future, we can see that the line that crosses through the 2010 low (3) and the 2018 crest (D) is at about 1.334 in March 2026, which is at the beginning of the narrowed-down time target range and at the lower edge of the price target span for the 4-year cycle crest. This area could be the area where the 4-year long-term cycle peaks out.
  1224→
  1225→## BIAS
  1226→
  1227→My bias is that the Euro will remain in a long-term bullish trend until at least the upcoming 4-year cycle crest, which is due to unfold sometime in the narrowed-down time frame of March–June 2026. We should then get a correction down to the 4-year cycle trough, expected, at the latest, by August 2027. However, once the 4-year cycle bottom is cemented, the prices should, if history repeats itself, continue higher within the next 4-year cycle to a combined 8 and 16-year cycle crest. However, we must be on the alert that the 16-year cycle peak could already manifest at this forthcoming 4-year cycle top (anticipated sometime between March–June 2026). If, against my bias, the prices were now to decline below the 1.014 low of February 2025 (6), then the current 24-month cycle would turn into a bearish trend, confirming that the 24-month cycle crest is behind us. The lowest price of this ongoing intermediate-term cycle will be at its very end, sometime between August 2026 and August 2027. Nevertheless, we would only have the confirma tion that the whole 16-year cycle has turned bearish if the 0.953 low of September 2022 (5) is broken. If this were to occur, then we might even need to revise the whole long-term chart labeling for the Euro, where the current 16-year cycle would more likely have started in January 2017.

  1231→## THE SWISS FRANC
  1232→
  1233→by Gianni Di Poce, MMA Analyst

  1235→## REVIEW
  1236→
  1237→The Swiss Franc in 2025 was exceptionally strong as it rallied to its highest level since 2011. The high of the year was on September 17, 2025, at 1.2904, and the low of the year was on February 3, 2025, at 1.0923. Once again, the Swiss Franc was one of the strongest-performing fiat currencies of 2025, and that’s even with the Swiss National Bank (SNB) cutting rates back down to zero. This clearly was not enough to reduce demand for this safe-haven currency. In a world filled with geopolitical turmoil, the neutrality of Switzerland has been very appealing to investors. But perhaps the biggest development of 2025 was the reset of an 8.25-year cycle. The big ques tion, however, is whether this cycle low occurred in May 2024 at 1.0899 or in February 2025 at 1.0923. Note how this February 2025 low occurred in the 6–22 month secondary low window that often occurs at long-term cycle bottoms. Forecast 2025’s conclusion section stated, “If the Swiss Franc is in a newer 8.25-year cycle from May 2024, then a rally as high as 1.2750 +/–.0150 cannot be ruled out. The biggest thing is that we expect either a high above the high of 2024 at 1.2036 or a low below the low of 2024 at 1.0900.” This long-term cyclical reset could prove to be a major tail wind for the Swiss Franc in the coming years, and points to higher prices.   1242→
  1243→## THE LONG-TERM CYCLES IN THE SWISS FRANC
  1244→
  1245→The Swiss Franc’s longest cycle is 16.5 years. While this cycle has been shown to fit well for this currency, there have only been two previous occurrences, which means it doesn’t have the strongest statistical reliability. Nonetheless, previous lows occurred in February 1985, July 2001, and then again in December 2016. Note that although there are three lows, they make up only two cycles, since they are measured low-to-low. The July 2001 bottom was at 0.5492, and the December 2016 low occurred at 0.9669. This means the next 16.5-year cycle trough in the Swiss Franc is due in 2032 +/– 3 years. But perhaps the most exciting development with respect to the 16.5-year cycle is how prices hit a new cycle high in 2025. This high in the 9th year is a strong signal that this is a bullish 16.5-year cycle. Forecast 2025 stated, “… ample time remains for new highs in this currency. Not to mention, a Republican president will be in the White House starting in 2025, and historically, this corresponds with a weaker Dollar, which means that the Swiss Franc could yet make new cycle highs.” And indeed, new highs followed. The 16.5-year cycle typically breaks down into two 8.25-year cycles. Historically, this has manifested as a two-phase pattern, with each phase lasting approximately 8.25 years. However, the current 16.5-year cycle may not be breaking down accordingly this time. It could be exhibiting three 5.5-year
  1246→
  1247→<!-- PAGE 151 END -->
  1248→
  1249→cycles, too, but this is not our bias. The previous 8.25-year cycle lows were in July 2001 (100 months from March 1993), November 2008 (88 months from July 2001), and December 2016 (96 months from November 2008). The 8.25-year cycle has historically shown a range of 88–100 months. Given this range, there are two possible scenarios for an 8.25-year cycle trough. The February 2025 low would have been 98 months from the December 2016 low, but then there’s also the May 1, 2024, low, which was 89 months from December 2016. Either way, there is strong evidence that a long-term cyclical reset took place in the Swiss Franc. In January 2026 will either enter the 11th month in a slightly newer 8.25-year cycle in the Swiss Franc from the February 2025 low, or it will begin the 20th month from the May 2024 low. Under the February 2025 labeling, the next 8.25-year cycle low wouldn’t be due until June 2032–June 2033. Note how this overlaps with the time band for the greater 16.5-year cycle. This is to be expected as it’s in the second 8.25-year cycle phase within the 16.5-year cycle. Under the May 2024 labeling, the low wouldn’t be due until September
  1250→
  1251→## 2031-September 2032.
  1252→
  1253→Next, the possibility of a 5.5-year cycle must be addressed. To be clear, there haven’t been any instances of a 5.5-year cycle going back to 1985. However, cycles are known to break down into smaller phases that are divided by two or three of the greater cycle length. Plus, 5.5-year cycles are observed in other currency markets. In this scenario, November 2022 would have been a 5.5-year cycle bottom. January 2026 would begin the 38th month from November 2022, or the 4th year, and there would still be time for new highs, although a crest could easily form in 2026. This is only the second 5.5-year cycle phase within the greater 16.5-year cycle, and a low would be due between May 2027 and May 2029. The 5.5-year cycle phase to follow out of such a low could easily be bearish since the 16.5-year cycle would be very late then, but it’s too soon to know for sure. The other long-term factor to consider in the Swiss Franc is the two-phase pattern to the 8.25year cycle, which is made up of two 4-year cycles. The 4-year cycle would have reset with the 8.25year cycle, which means that the Swiss Franc is now in the first 4-year cycle phase in this newer 8.25-year cycle. 2026 would either begin the 1st or 2nd year of this 4-year cycle phase, depending on
  1254→
  1255→<!-- PAGE 152 END -->
  1256→
  1257→whether the greater 8.25-year cycle bottomed in May 2024 or February 2025. Note that the previous 4-year cycle exhibited a case of contraction, as the prior low was in November 2022. But such cases of contraction are not uncommon when longer cycles come due, as the 8.25-year cycle overpowers the 4-year cycle. It’s still early enough in this 4-year cycle for the Swiss Franc to climb to new highs, and in all likelihood, into the 1.3200 +/– .0200 zone at least.
  1258→
  1259→## GEOCOSMICS
  1260→
  1261→From a mundane astrological standpoint, one of the risks for the Swiss Franc in 2026 is that the Swiss National Bank may struggle to keep interest rates low if inflation resurges. Between Neptune making its definitive ingress into Aries starting on January 26, 2026, and Jupiter’s eventual ingress into Leo on June 30, and the subsequent trine between the two planets on July 20, there’s a real threat of another inflationary wave in 2026. However, this may turn out to be bullish for the Swiss Franc, because it would eventually force the Swiss National Bank to raise interest rates again. Keep in mind that rates have been cut back to zero in Switzerland, and this hasn’t been enough to stem the rise in the Swiss Franc. It’s not my bias that the Swiss National Bank hikes in 2026, but if they were to begin considering rate hikes again, it probably wouldn’t be before the Jupiter–Pluto opposition of August 31. Transits to the Swiss National Bank’s natal chart can also be considered. The central bank was established on June 19, 1906, by the National Bank Act, but it didn’t start operating until June 16, 1907. There is no birthtime available, but outer planetary aspects can still be analyzed. The location of this chart is Zurich, Switzerland. Forecast 2025 stated, “The first planetary placement that stands out is the SNB’ s natal Venus at 29 degrees of Taurus. Not only is the 29th degree of a sign considered to be karmically potent, but Venus also rules currencies. It’ s no surprise that the Swiss Franc is one of the strongest currencies from a historical standpoint, with Venus in Taurus, a sign she rules. But in 2025 and into 2026, we will see Uranus transit over this degree on multiple occasions. Uranus will go retrograde and direct within the orb of Venus as well. Transiting Uranus conjunct Venus is a classical currency boom or bust signature. Thus, we have the geocosmic catalyst here for the Swiss Franc to potentially collapse as low as 1.0200 +/– 0.0100 in 2025 for an 8.25-year cycle low. A sharp rally would likely follow given the nature of this transit. But in the event it’ s a newer 8.25-year cycle from May 1, 2024, we could see the Swiss Franc explode higher in value, and potentially rally as high as 1.2750 +/– .0150 in 2025. This scenario is supported by the political cycle as well. Ura nus will hit the 29-degree mark of Taurus in June 2025, which is a bit late given the 88–100-month cycle range of the Swiss Franc’ s 8.25-year cycle. If the low is complete below, then it could coincide with a surge higher.” The newer 8.25-year cycle scenario was in play, and indeed, the Swiss Franc exploded higher just above the upside target of 1.2750 +/– .0150 last year. The high of the year was in September 2025 at 1.2904. Looking ahead into 2026, there are a few notable transits that stand out in the SNB’s natal chart. First, there will be both Saturn and Jupiter returns for the central bank. The Saturn return is very early in the year, January 13. The Jupiter return occurs a couple of times due to retrograde motions on February 15 and April 3. If anything, these conjunctions will serve to further reinforce the value of the Swiss Franc for the first few months of 2026. There will even be another conjunction with transiting Uranus over the Swiss Franc’s natal Venus on April 23. This may serve to coincide with another notable surge in the value of the Swiss Franc +/- 1 month. However, the prospect for volatility in the Swiss Franc starts to increase starting in May, as there will be a T-square between Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune. Transiting Saturn will be at the apex, as
  1262→

  1264→
  1265→Uranus and Neptune are in opposition in the SNB’s natal chart, in Capricorn and Cancer, respectively. Due to retrograde motions, there will be another passage of this T-square in late September and early October. Thus, the Swiss Franc may experience a period of sharp volatility between late May and early October. It could start as an initial spike to the upside, followed by a sharp drop to the downside, or vice versa, but this seems to be the hot spot for the currency in 2026. Remember that if the mar ket sniffs out that the SNB is going to eventually start raising rates again, it could lead to a flood of money rushing into this safe-haven currency. It’s also worth pointing out that the Uranus–Pluto trine, which is the feature signature of 2026 and beyond, does not aspect the Swiss National Bank chart at all throughout this year. If anything, this may prove to provide some extra stability, which is highly sought after in this current market environment.
  1266→
  1267→## CONCLUSIONS
  1268→
  1269→There are still questions as to whether the Swiss Franc is breaking down into a two-phase, a three-phase, or even a combination pattern when it comes to the 16.5-year cycle. As of this writ ing in November 2025, my bias is increasingly that a combination pattern with both 8.25-year and 5.5-year cycle phases is playing out. The breakout to new multi-year highs in 2025 confirmed that an 8.25-year cycle bottomed either in May 2024 or February 2025 (the latter can be considered a double-bottom, or secondary low). The Swiss Franc is still early enough in the 8.25-year cycle for the currency to exceed the 2025 highs in 2026. However, it’s not as probable that a sustained surge similar to what was witnessed in 2025 will play out in 2026. The 5.5-year cycle is still early enough to carry the Swiss Franc to new multi-year highs as well. Ideally, a rally up to the 1.3900–1.4000 zone can occur before the longer-term 16.5-year cycle tops out, and while this is the best-case scenario for the Swiss Franc in 2026, it’s not the likeliest one. Instead, a rally up to the 1.3400–1.3600 area is the preferred target for 2026. My bias is that the Swiss Franc won’t see lower prices than 1.2200–1.2300 in 2026 either. In other words, new highs above the 2025 highs are on the table, but new lows below the 2025 lows are not (that would be quite the reversal back lower). In fact, the sooner the Swiss Franc breaks above 1.2600–1.2700, the sooner that becomes the new floor, or the new support zone in this currency. It’s shaping up to be another strong year for the Swiss Franc in 2026. In summary, position traders may buy the Swiss Franc as long as it remains above 1.1950 on a closing basis.

  1280→
  1281→## REVIEW AND PREVIEW
  1282→
  1283→Bitcoin had quite a year in 2025. It started with a new all-time high of 109,071 on January 26. It then fell to a yearly low of 74,445 on April 7–9, a loss of 31.7%. Next, it rallied to yet another new all-time high (ATH) on October 6, 2025, at 126,223, which was a double top to an earlier ATH of 124,480 made on August 14, 2025. The behavior of Bitcoin (BTC) during the year fit the two special updates I issued during the year. The first was issued on May 5 as BTC was trading around 94,000. It called for an all-time high to take place around October 2025, +/– 1 month, based on the history of the halving cycle, where new ATHs tend to happen 16–18 months later. The halving event took place in April 2024. The high was thus due August–October. The forecast was moved up one month, to September–November, based on the phasing of shorter-term cycles and geocosmic studies. The price target given for the high was up to 150,000–158,000. After the 124,480 new ATH on August 14 and a pullback to the 105,000 area on September 1, a special webinar was conducted on September 14, where my outlook on Bitcoin was revised. Although 150,000 was still a possible target, it was getting late in the time band for a new ATH, ideally due in October now. Traders needed to be alert to a possible double top this late in the cycle, where BTC could test and even slightly exceed the 124,480 ATH on August 14, and that is what happened. On October 6, 2025, the yearly high in BTC, as of this writing, was recorded at 126,223. The combination of cycles studies, geocosmics, and chart patterns worked out extremely well. Since that time, and as of this writing in early November, BTC has declined by over 20% and below 100,000. Based on these same cycle studies reported in the special update and webinar of May and Sep tember 2025, the outlook now calls for a decline of 70–90% in BTC by the end of 2026. A new ATH in the first quarter of 2026 would alter or delay this bearish outlook for 2026.

   743→## THE NASDAQ IN 2026
   744→
   745→by Wiebke Held, MMA Analyst
   746→
   747→## INTRODUCTION
   748→
   749→This year, MMA is pleased to provide a yearly outlook on the NASDAQ Composite by MMTA Director and MMAAnalyst Wiebke Held. Many of the longer-term cycles will match well with those of the DJIA, although their actual completions will often be slightly apart from one another in weeks or even months.
   750→
   751→## REVIEW AND PREVIEW
   752→
   753→The NASDAQ Composite Index started the year with a retest on January 24, 2025, of the all-time high that was printed on December 16, 2024. This all-time high of 20,205 was the 3-year cycle crest that formed after a remarkable 100% gain following the lows that formed in October 2022, which was the 6-year cycle trough. The retest of the all-time highs occurred again (triple top) on February 18, which then marked the start of a quick and steep decline into the expected 3-year cycle trough, which formed on April 7, 2025, at 14,784. The 3-year cycle trough was followed by an equally steep and quick rally with only shallow pullbacks. As expected in the first phases of new cycles, they are extremely bullish. And as of this writing, the NASDAQ is still making new highs. In 2026, we are now reaching the time band for the first 50-week cycle trough within the new 3-year cycle, which will likely be followed by another rally into the crest of the second 50-week phase of the 3-year cycle. But traders and investors must be on the lookout, as this current 3-year cycle is the last phase of the current 6- and 9-year cycles, and those are the last phase of the current 18-year cycle. With long-term cycles being in their last phase, and intermediate-term cycles entering their sec ond phase in 2026, the likelihood of the 18-year crest forming in 2026 is high, which would be the start of the decline into the 18-year cycle trough. For both the long- and intermediate-term cycles analysis, the NASDAQ Composite Index (Ticker: IXIC) is used, since this index provides the most historical data available. In the following sections, I will refer to the NASDAQ Composite Index as the “NASDAQ.”
   754→
   755→## LONG-TERM CYCLES
   756→

The progress (middle column) is measured as of early November 2025. This is the preferred path and labeling.

   762→
   763→## The 18-Year Cycle
   764→
   765→Since the NASDAQ started trading in 1971, there have been three prominent lows in 1974, 1990, and 2009 that suggest an 18-year cycle is present in the NASDAQ. Measured across 100% of the instances of the 18-year cycle, its normal length is 17.3 years with an orb of 17 months. Measured from its start in March 2009, the NASDAQ will be entering its 17th year of the 18-year cycle in early 2026. The 18-year cycle trough is due 2024–2027. So as of 2026, we are now in the third year of the time band for the 18-year cycle trough. There are 3 lows and 2 completed cycles of the 18-year cycle in the history of the NASDAQ so far. The past data suggest that the NASDAQ is following the same long-term cycle rhythm as the Dow Jones and S&P500 indices. Thus, we use the March 2009 low as the 18-year cycle low even though the low in 2002 was lower. Historically, the 18-year cycle has rallied from its starting low to its crest for 161 months on average, with a range of 113–180 months before the crest forms. Since March 2009, the NASDAQ has rallied for 198 months and is still making new all-time highs as of this writing in November 2025. This is the longest period of increase in its history. The appreciation from trough to crest has historically been 788–1489%, with an average gain of 1139%. The appreciation from the low in March 2009 until late October 2025 has been over 1680%, again the largest appreciation in its history. Being well into the time band for the 18-year cycle trough and seeing an extension beyond the historical boundaries of time, going up and appreciation, led me to conclude that the 18-year cycle crest is imminent. Declines from the crest to the trough have historically lasted 13–108 months with an average of 61 months. The decline into the 18-year cycle from 1974 to 1990 lasted 13 months, and the decline
   766→
   767→<!-- PAGE 113 END -->
   768→
   769→into the 18-year cycle from 1990 to 2009 lasted 103 months. If we count the months from the last 18-year cycle crest in March 2000 to the low in October 2002, the decline lasted 30 months, before a double bottom in 2009 stretched this period longer. Hence, one could argue that a more normal length of decline into an 18-year cycle trough lasts from 13 to 30 months. The depreciation from the crest to the trough has ranged from 34%–75% with an average decline of 55%. The current 18-year cycle is breaking down into a combination pattern with lows at the 1/3 (6-year cycle) and 1/2 marks (9-year cycle). Let’s explore the phases of the 18-year cycle next to refine this market timing projection.
   770→
   771→## The 9-Year Cycle
   772→
   773→In the history of the NASDAQ, there are 5 completed instances of the 9-year cycle, which is the half-cycle to the 18-year cycle. The 9-year cycle has a mean periodicity of 9.5 years and a normal length of 8–11 years. The last 9-year cycle trough happened in March 2020 when the COVID-19 pandemic hit, and slightly expanded to 11 years and 1 month. Measured from the March 2020 low, the current 9-year cycle is in its 6th year. The next 9-year cycle trough is due between January 2028 and April 2031. One may notice that this time band does not overlap with the 18-year cycle time band. We at MMA know that cycles tend to balance out over time. Hence, I expect the current 9-year cycle to be on the shorter side in length or even contract (6–8 years), as the first 9-year cycle was slightly on the longer side and thus expanded somewhat. The current 9-year cycle is breaking down into a 3-phase pattern with 3-year cycle lows (range 26–36 months) in October 2022 and April 2025. We are now in the third 3-year cycle which is the final phase of the current 9-year cycle, when the low of the 9-year cycle would normally be due. Since 1971, all but one 9-year cycle exhibited a right translation, meaning the crest formed past the mid-point of the cycle, which is a bullish trend characteristic. Historically, bullish 9-year cycles have peaked between 79–132 months with an average of 98 months. As of this writing in November 2025, the current 9-year cycle has been going up for 68 months from its start in March 2020. The appreciation of bullish 9-year cycles has been between 207%–642% with an average of 421%. Based on this study, the price target for the current 9-year cycle crest is 34,700 with a range of 20,500–49,400. The current 9-year cycle has appreciated over 260% so far and is well within that range. The historical range of decline from the crest to trough in bullish 9-year cycles has been 1–15 months, with an average of 8 months. The historical depreciation in all cases has seen a range of 29%–75% with an average of 40%. Since we are in the third and final 3-year cycle phase of two 9-year cycles within the greater 18-year cycle, the next 9-year cycle trough will also be the 18-year cycle trough. Thus, we anticipate a 29–75% decline once the crest is in.
   774→
   775→## The 6-Year Cycle
   776→
   777→In the history of the NASDAQ, 8 completed instances of the 6-year cycle can be observed at the 1/3 intervals of the greater 18-year cycle. The 6-year cycle has a mean periodicity of 5.5 years and a normal length of 4–7 years. The last 6-year cycle trough culminated in October 2022. Measured from this low, the current 6-year cycle is in its 3rd year. This is the third and final 6-year cycle within the current 18-year cycle.
   778→
   779→<!-- PAGE 114 END -->
   780→
   781→The current 6-year cycle is exhibiting a breakdown into a 2-phase pattern (3-year cycle low in April 2025) with bullish characteristics (higher highs and higher lows). Since 1971, all 6-year cycles exhibited a bullish right translation pattern. Historically, 6-year cycles have rallied from trough to crest between 39–76 months with an average of 61 months. As of this writing in November 2025, the current 6-year cycle has been going up for 37 months from its start in October 2022. The appreciation of 6-year cycles has been between 116%–409% with an average of 241%. Based on these studies, the price target for the 6-year cycle crest is 34,300 with a range of 21,700–51,200. The current 6-year cycle has appreciated over 139% so far and is well within the target range already. The historical range of decline from the crest to trough in all instances of the 6-year cycle has been 1–31 months, with an average of 12 months. The historical depreciation has seen a range of 20%–78% with an average of 38%. Since we are in the third and final of three 6-year cycles within the greater 18-year cycle, the next 6-year cycle trough will also be the 9-year cycle and 18-year cycle trough. Summarizing the long-term cycle review, traders and investors must be alert to the possibility of a long-term cycle crest forming at any time now, as the 18-year cycle has already exceeded its historical range of time going up and appreciation. Thus, 2026 will likely be the year in which we will see the 18-year cycle crest forming. Looking at the sub-cycles of the 18-year cycle, we enter the time band for the crest to form within the next 2–11 months, when the 9-year and 6-year cycles start to enter their historical ranges. Both cycles have already entered the price target range for their crests. As long as price remains above the 22- and 33-month moving average on the monthly chart and the market is making new highs, we have not seen the 18-year cycle crest yet. The price target range for the crest, where the 9- and 6-year cycle price targets overlap, is 21,700–49,400. Once the crest is in, there will be a steep decline into the 18-year cycle trough, which is due in the next 2 years, and more specifically, where the time bands of the 18- and 6-year cycles overlap (February 2027–August 2027). The decline will likely last between 1 and 31 months, with a depreciation of 33%–78% from the crest.
   782→
   783→## INTERMEDIATE-TERM CYCLES
   784→
   785→Let’s now further analyze the intermediate-term cycles, as each long-term cycle contains smaller sub-cycles (the MMA principle of “cycles within cycles”), enabling us to make more refined market timing projections by breaking down and following these sub-cycles and formulate a trading plan for 2026.
   786→
   787→## Cycle Start / Progress Next Due
