   553→## NATIONAL AND LOCAL SECURITY
   554→
   555→Almost every issue of importance confronting the United States today can be associated with the Aries V ortex, where the Saturn–Neptune conjunction falls on the U.S. descendant and squares its natal Venus (chart ruler) on the midheaven. It also pertains to the Uranus–Pluto trine in early air signs, which makes up the sides of the funnel, and whose midpoint also falls on 0° Aries with Saturn and Neptune. Additionally, transiting Uranus and Pluto make a grand trine to the early Libra rising in this newly rectified chart. Let us start with the issue of trust, an important factor in the status of America’s exceptionalism. Trust falls under the domain of Neptune. But Neptune is compromised via its conjunction with Sat urn, which is not trust, but rather skepticism, which can easily turn to distrust and even separation if one of the parties in a relationship feels that the agreement or precedents supporting the relationship are being changed without its approval and consent. Relationships are the key to this current chart because the Saturn–Neptune conjunction is on the cusp of the 7th house, which rules partnerships and allies. Furthermore, both Saturn and Neptune square the U.S. Venus in Cancer. Venus also rules one’s partnerships and allies, those who support the nation and have been loyal to it. All of this support and trust has been upended since March, when first Neptune, and then Sat urn, moved into Aries, forming these powerful aspects to the U.S. chart. The White House suddenly announced huge tariffs on nations that export its goods to the U.S. Aside from causing a mini-panic in financial markets in early April (Venus rules the stock market), this abrupt disruption of longstanding precedence in trade and international relationships has led many of the U.S. allies to seek other nations to fill in the gap of lost trade relations with the U.S. It’s not like they completely stopped trading with the U.S., for developing new alliances and trading partners take time. But these changing trade relationships are underway as we enter 2026, for many nations no longer trust the U.S. to honor its precedents. They fear (Saturn) that abrupt, non-consensual changes can and will happen again, and in many cases, may be due to some act or statement on their part that personally offends the President. This is perhaps the leading reason why America is losing its status of exceptionalism in the eyes of the world. It takes a long time to build up trust. It takes only a moment to break it. Without trust, you do not have the foundation for a healthy relationship. America has now jeopardized its relationship with many of its historic allies. It will be interesting to see if it can recapture that trust before those other nations develop new trading alliances. The consequences of these heavy-handed unilateral trade decisions have also led the charge for the currencies of other multinational alliances (like BRICS) to compete with the U.S. Dollar as an acceptable standard world currency for trade. Again, this relates to the nation’s Venus being besieged by Saturn and Neptune. Venus represents a nation’s currency, and the U.S. Dollar has been falling in value as of January 2025. Despite these challenges indicated by Saturn and Neptune, the transits of Uranus and Pluto, making a grand trine with this revised U.S. Ascendant, hold much promise. The U.S. is still a world leader in technology and innovation. With Uranus transiting back to its natal sign of Gemini, this techno-renaissance is likely to continue. More discoveries and new applications with technology are forecasted throughout this decade, and especially in 2026. However, Uranus in Gemini has also corresponded to deadly wars for the U.S. in every past instance. Technology and innovation have led to economic booms, but in many cases, these discoveries and applications were brought about due to war entanglements. This might actually help the U.S. in its military campaigns, but there is still

   636→
   637→## INTRODUCTION
   638→
   639→The U.S. stock market has been on a tear for the past 17 years, following its 72-year cycle low of March 6–9, 2009, at the height of the Great Recession, when the DJIA had dropped 54.4% from its then all-time high made just 17 months earlier, in October 2007. The low in March 2009 was 6470 in the DJIA. By the end of October 2025 (as this is being written), it was trading at a new all-time high of 48,040, a gain of over 742% in 16.5 years, which isn’t bad. It demonstrates how wealth is built in the stock market via knowledge of investing and cycle studies during long-term cycle troughs. Along the way, however, there have been seven cases of 16% or greater declines in the DJIA, with the steepest being the 37% one-month decline from February 2020 to March 2020, during the outbreak of the COVID-19 pandemic. That is a lot of steep sell-offs in just 18 years (2007–2025). They ranged in intervals of 1–4 years from one another as follows: 1. March 2009 54.4% decline from high of October 2007 2. October 2011 (31 mo) 19.2% decline from high of May 2011 3. August 2015 (46 mo) 16.2% decline from high of May 2015 4. December 2018 (40 mo) 19.4% decline from the high of October 2018 5. March 2020 (15 mo) 37.1% decline from high of February 2020 6. October 2022 (31 mo) 22.4% decline from high of January 2022 7. April 2025 (30 mo) 18.8% decline from high of December 2024
   640→
   641→<!-- PAGE 102 END -->
   642→
   643→Of the seven completed cases of 16% or greater declines since the then all-time high of October 2007, six have lasted 30–46 months. The outlier was 2020’s pandemic low at only a 15-month interval. That was indeed an outlier in many ways. If the next 16+% decline happens in the 30–46 month interval, it would occur from October 2027 to February 2029. As will be demonstrated shortly, that falls within the time band of several cycles, including the important 18-year cycle trough, a genera tional low that is due 2022–2030. Yet, when one looks at the long-term history of the DJIA (as illustrated in The Ultimate Book on Stock Market Timing, Volume 1: Cycles and Patterns in the Indexes 1), the picture is concerning, because 1) the low to a high in the 18-year cycle has lasted 6–20 years in all 12 completed cases to date, and 2) in 11 of those 12 cases, the rally lasted 9–20 years. As 2026 begins, it will mark the 17th year that this cycle has been overall bullish, which makes it in the mature stage of its 18-year cycle. The peak of the 18-year cycle is due at any time now, followed by the low, which is also due any time by 2030. Historically, though, the crest has been 17 years or greater in three of those 12 cases, for only a 25% frequency. However, all three cases of these short but steep declines have occurred within the four cases since the Great Depression of 1932, which was the prior 72-year cycle. This means bull markets have lasted 17–20 years in 75% of the four most recent cases. This will be the 4th time in the last five cases that it has lasted at least 17 years, and three of the prior four bull runs have lasted 18–20 years. The cycle top is due. It’s as if you know you are this close, but also that far away, from an important top, after which the stock market historically falls at least 37%. The frequency of a 37% or greater decline happening by 2030 is about 83% (10 of 12 cases). And in eight of those cases, the decline was between 37.5 and 63.6%. Only once was the decline less than 30% (in 1953). And only twice was it greater than 63.6%. Since this next 18-year cycle low is not expected to be part of a greater cycle, the range of 37.5–63.6% is the projected drop off from the current all-time high that is due. If it falls more than 63.6%, or even more than the 54.4% decline into the long-term cycle low of March 2009, then an even longer-term 90-year cycle must be considered. That degree of decline has only occurred twice in
   644→
   645→<!-- PAGE 103 END -->
   646→
   647→U.S. stocks: into the lows of 1842 and 1932. If the 90-year cycle is to occur a third time, it would be due within 15 years of 2022, and probably within 10 years of 2022 (by 2032), based on the long-term Saturn–Uranus conjunction taking place on June 28, 2032. Our studies have shown that the greatest percentage of long-term stock market cycles have occurred near a Saturn–Uranus conjunction or opposition than any other planetary pair cycle. The takeaway from this introduction is that the DJIA is due to top out any time before 2029, and most likely between 2026 and 2029. However, there is just as strong a probability that the 18-year cycle low will happen October 2027–January 2029, and the crest would happen before then. The challenge is: how much before then? Since 1932, there have been no bear markets at the end of the 18-year cycle that lasted more than two years. Two of them lasted less than one year. The shortest on record was the 40% decline in just two months from August to October 1987. It is this author’s opinion that under President Donald Trump, we will see another instance of a steep and brief bear market lasting less than two years, and probably less than one year. Nevertheless, a decline of 37–63% will offer a generational opportunity to build wealth via the stock market for those who are willing to be patient for 9–20 years afterwards, which could yield a return between 300% and 800%. Now, let’s see if we can add more pieces of the current stock market puzzle in the quest to narrow the time band for both the crest and the trough. For if we can, that guidance can mean the difference between a very healthy and profitable investment on the horizon versus one that could be meager if entering at the wrong time (too early or too late) or one that could even spell a severe loss if not careful and aware of the cycle messages ahead.
   648→
   649→## CYCLES: LONG-TERM
   650→
   651→We begin this section with a review of long-term cycles (low to low) in the DJIA. The 18-Year Cycle: The last 18-, 36-, and 72-year cycles started with the low of March 6–9, 2009. Our focus will be on the 18-year cycle, as that is the longest cycle currently coming due, from 2024 to 2030. Since it is the first phase of longer cycles, it is not expected to be as steep a decline as happened into the low of March 2009, which was 54.4% in the DJIA. However, as noted earlier, over 80% of 18-year cycles have declined 37–63%, so this remains our price target for this important cycle. Time-wise, the crest is due any time before the end of 2029. The low will follow and is due at any time before the end of 2030. Historically, the price appreciation from the start of the 18-year cycle to its crest has been 122– 778%. However, since 1914, it has gained 320–778%. Measured from the start of the current cycle at 6470, the upside price target for the crest is 27,174–56,807. As of this writing, the DJIA is in the upper part of this range, nearing 50,000. Thus, the time and price criteria for the 18-year cycle crest are being met. The final high is due at any time. The 9-Year Cycle: All cycles break down into divisions of 2 and 3, and sometimes both. The halfcycle (9-year cycle) to the 18-year cycle has a range of 7.5–10.5 years. The 9-year half-cycle time band has coincided with a prominent trough in 10 of the 12 cases to date in the 18-year cycle, with some slight distortions. The March 2020 pandemic low, for instance, was exactly 11 years following the start of the 18-year cycle, and although slightly outside of our normal range, it will be considered a 9-year half-cycle. If correct, the second 9-year half-cycle is next due September 2027–September 2030.
   652→
   653→<!-- PAGE 104 END -->
   654→
   655→Price-wise, in all but two of these cases, the crest of the second half of the 18-year cycle was considerably higher than the crest of the first half. That is the case again now. The 6-Year Cycle: The six-year cycle is a 1/3 division of the 18-year cycle. It has a normal range of 5–7 years, but can expand to eight years in the second or third phase. In all 12 cases of the 18-year cycle, there has been a 5–7-year cycle low in the first phase. However, the current 18-year cycle is now in its third phase. The first phase was a double bottom in August 2015 and February 2016, which was 6–7 years following the start of the cycle in March 2009. The second phase was the low on October 13, 2022, again 6–7 years after the first phase trough. Allowing a range of 5–8 years, the final phase will be due 2027–2030. The measured price targets for the crest of this third 6-year cycle phase are 47,500 +/– 4842 and 50,244 +/– 4115. The overlap is 46,128–52,342. Once completed, we will look for a decline of 37–63%. We would also look for prices to fall to or below the 108-month moving average shown on the monthly chart.
   656→
   657→## CYCLES: INTERMEDIATE-TERM

   659→## Cycle Start/Progress Next Due

   670→
   671→Within the longer-term 9- and 6-year cycles, the DJIA also subdivides into two or three phases. The current 9-year cycle has been exhibiting three 3-year phases. The 6-year cycle can also be sub divided into two 3-year phases or three 2-year sub-cycles. Both share in common a 3-year cycle. This often happens with “combination cycles,” and this 18-year cycle is a combination of 9-year and 6-year cycle phases. They share in common a 3-year cycle with a range of 30–42 months, which MMAAnalyst Ulric Aspegrén calls a “keystone cycle,” which means it is a subdivision of two in one cycle branch and a subdivision of three in another. It is for this reason that we will focus on the 3-year cycle and not the 4-year (or even 4.5-year) cycles of our longer-term studies. Besides, the three-year cycle has been more reliable than the 4-year cycle over the past 50 years. Following the 9-year cycle low of March 2020, the DJIA has exhibited 3-year cycle lows in October 2022 (31 months) and April 2025 (30 months). The April 2025 low was the second of three 3-year phases to the 9-year cycle. It was also the first of two 3-year cycles troughs that make up the 6-year cycle that began in October 2022. Thus, the next 3-year cycle low is on schedule to complete not only the 9- and 6-year cycles, but the entire 18-year cycle. If we measure 30–42 months following the low of April 7, 2025, we get an ideal time band for all four cycles (18-, 9-, 6-, and 3-year) due between October 2027 and October 2028. However, we have to be careful because when longer-term cycles are due, the shorter-term cycles (phases) within them can distort (contract or expand) beyond their normal time bands.
   672→
   673→<!-- PAGE 105 END -->
   674→
   675→I began this chapter with the study of the seven declines of 16% or greater since the 72-year cycle crest of October 2007. To repeat, “Of the seven complete cases of 16% or greater declines since the then all-time high of October 2007, six have lasted 30–46 months. If the next 16+% decline happens in the 30–46 month interval, it would occur October 2027–February 2029.” It overlaps nicely with the 18-, 9-, 6-, and 3-year cycles. Our formal studies on price gains and losses in The Ultimate Book on Stock Market Timing, Volume 1: Cycles and Patterns in the Indexes 1 were conducted on 4–year cycles. However, since Table 2 showed a 4-year cycle low that also began April 7, 2025, and its next low is also due during the 2028 +/– 1 year time band, we can apply those studies to the current market and calculate a price target for the crest of all these cycles. First of all, these studies show that the vast majority of rallies from the low to the high of a 4-year cycle last 12–49 months with a price appreciation of 70–189%. This would mean that the crest will 1) likely occur after March 2026 and 2) could soar to 62,240–105,800. However, there is a caveat. This is the last 3-year cycle phase of 6- and 9-year cycles, which are in their last phase of the greater 18-year cycle. The percentage of appreciation in the last 4-year cycle phases of an 18-year cycle, in our formal studies, was not so great. It ranged from a gain of only 29% to 83% in six of the seven cases since 1893. That would yield an upside price target of only 47,225–67,000. This is interesting because it overlaps with our measured upside price calculation of the 9-year cycle at 49,400–57,750 and the 6-year cycle at 51,609–56,481. Earlier, we calculated that the 18-year cycle crest would rise to 27,174–56,807, and the six-year cycle to 46,128–52,342. It may be too much to expect, but all four of these price calculations overlap 51,609–52,342. The final intermediate-term cycle we consider is the 50-week type, with a normal range of 34–67 weeks. Usually, there will be three of these phases within a 3-year cycle. April 7, 2025, began the first 50-week (and 3-year) cycle. It is due to bottom with 16.5 weeks of March 27, 2026, or December 1, 2025–July 17, 2026. But this will only be the first of three 50-week cycles before the final 3-, 6-, 9-, and 18-year cycles come due. In fact, there could even be more or fewer than three 50-week phases here since this is the last stage of so many greater cycles converging, which is when distortions most often occur. The timing is never easy when very long-term generational bottoms unfold. Investors need to develop a buy-in plan whenever the DJIA falls more than 35% off its all-time high, which could begin as early as 2026. For now, our immediate trading plan calls for a buying opportunity within 16 weeks of March 27, 2026, and with a decline of at least 8%. Yet, if the next 50-week cycle rally only makes a double top to the high of this current 50-week cycle, or stalls within an upside price target range given above, investors must be prepared for a powerful reversal to begin.

   677→## GEOCOSMIC CYCLES
   678→
   679→Our basic rule is that long-term cycle crests and troughs tend to unfold when major aspects involving long-term planetary pair cycles involving Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, or Pluto are in effect. We also consider the sign position of the Lunar North Node. We have two long-term planetary pair cycles in effect now. First and foremost is the 36-year synodic (conjunction) cycle of Saturn and Neptune, which came within 13’ of a degree of exactness in July 2025 and will be exact on February 20, 2026. Our studies reported in The Ultimate Book on Stock Market Timing Volume 2: Geocosmic Correlations to Investment Cycles 2 showed that long-term stock
   680→

   682→
   683→market cycles tended to top out within 11 months of the beginning through the end of this aspect, with all but one in 8 months or less. This means the long-term cycle crest could happen by October 2026. The second long-term planetary aspect is Uranus trine Pluto, which will transpire five times between July 2026 and May 2028. It was close enough in the middle of 2025 to be considered already underway (less than a degree from an exact trine). There are only three cases of trines between these two planets in the history of the DJIA. Two of them were 9-year cycle troughs. With an orb of 10 months on either side of the first or last passage, this fits well in a broad time band for the 18-year cycle as described previously. However, this is too wide a time band to be of any practical use. The Saturn–Neptune conjunction is more useful for identifying a possible 18-year cycle crest. Both Saturn and Neptune will make sextiles to Uranus and Pluto in 2025–2026. This is a favor able combination that could also help identify a long-term cycle crest whose time band is now in effect. Saturn makes three sextiles from April 4, 2025, to March 28, 2026. Neptune will sextile Uranus and Pluto from August 28, 2025, through June 6, 2027. The overlap of August 2025 through March 2026 stands out for an important reversal. It will likely be at least a 50-week cycle crest, but could also exhibit the first 50-week cycle trough. There is also a very significant cosmic arrangement taking place July 20–21, 2026, as mentioned in our brief note to traders at the beginning of this year’s book. This is when Jupiter will trine Nep tune, oppose Pluto, and be in sextile to Uranus. Within six months, and usually only two, the Jupiter– Neptune trine has a strong correlation to at least a 50-week cycle trough. The Jupiter sextile Uranus aspect is also similar to a propensity to identify a 50-week or greater cycle low within 4 months. However, the Jupiter/Pluto opposition is most important. It can be either an intermediate (or longer term) cycle low or high, or both, within six months. If it is a high, it takes place within only 4 months, and a powerful decline follows. This fits well with our outlook of the 18-year cycle crest unfolding in 2026, and ideally within four months of July 2026.
   684→
   685→## The Jupiter–Saturn Cycle
   686→
   687→Throughout history, intermediate or long–term cycle highs and lows in the U.S. stock market have related to the 20-year Jupiter–Saturn cycle as follows: During the conjunction, stock markets tend to make highs. 1–3 years later, near the first 1/8 phase (waxing semi-square) of the 20-year cycle, the U.S. stock market completes an intermediate-term cycle low. There is usually an international military war breaking out then as well. • The stock market tends to rally and form an important crest 3–6 years after the conjunction. • The stock market tends to suffer a serious decline, even a crash, 7–9 years after the conjunction. The Jupiter–Saturn conjunction occurred on December 20, 2020, and there indeed was a military crisis as the six-year stock market cycle trough occurred in October 2022 (1–3 years after the con junction). The market was then due to rally 3–6 years after that low, which brings us to 2023–2026, and indeed the market has rallied into this time band. The next step involves a serious decline, per haps a crash, into an important long-term cycle low due in 2027–2029. Once again, this aligns with the labeling of the long-term cycles according to the “Cycles Progress Table” given earlier. Our expectation is for the DJIA to lose 37–63% of its value from the high to the low during this period.

   935→## THE 18.5-YEAR CYCLE IN SILVER AND ITS PHASES
   936→
   937→The basic long-term cycle in Silver is 18.5 years, with a range of 15–22 years. The previous instance of this cycle was the double-bottom low of 1991–1993, when Silver fell to $3.51/ounce (February 1991 and February 1993) after its all-time high of $50.00/ounce in January 1980. The low of February 1991 occurred 19 years and three months after the prior 18.5-year cycle trough of November 1971. The next (and most recent) occurrence of this long-term cycle was in October 2008. That was 17 years and eight months later, as Silver fell from its crest of 21.44 in March 2008 to a low of 8.40 in October 2008, just as Saturn began its five-passage opposition to Uranus that lasted through mid-2010. This decline then led to a retest of the all-time high when Silver soared to 49.82 in April 2011. The next 18.5-year cycle is therefore due in 2027 +/– 3.5 years. In January 2026, we will be entering the 17th year and third month of the current cycle, which places us well within the orb of the 18.5-year cycle.

   947→## THE 6-YEAR CYCLE
   948→
   949→The 18.5-year cycle can also break down into three 6-year cycle phases, with a range of 5–7 years. The second phase was bearish and ended with the March 2020 low, five years and three months later. This would mean we are now in the third and final 6-year cyclical phase, which is expected to complete the longer 18.5year cycle in March 2026 +/– 12 months. The overlap with the contracted 9.25-year cycle discussed above is October 2026 to March 2027, which is the ideal time for the low. Therefore, 2026 will begin the 18th year of the longer-term 18.5-year cycle and the sixth year of its second 7- to 11-year half-cycle. The 18.5-year cycle low is due anytime in the next four and a half years. The 9.25-year cycle low is due over the next four years.    971→## CONCLUSIONS
   972→
   973→Last year’s Forecast 2025 book concluded: “The technical and fundamental picture remains strong for Silver, which could even record a new ATH at 53.06 +/– 5.27 within 3 months of the Sat urn–Neptune conjunction on February 20, 2026, before a sharp sell-off into 2027. As we saw in the previous 18.5-year cycle, the crest formed in March 2008, and the cycle culminated 7 months later in October after a 61% decline.” At the time of writing this report, Silver has just formed a new ATH on November 13 at 54.42. If this were not the 18.5-year cycle crest, I would expect it to form soon within the price target provided, and for it to be followed by a sharp move down. Of course, we never see a straight move down, and there is an intermediate 26-month cycle low due, from which I expect a corrective rally. While it is not my bias, Silver is very volatile, and we may see the rally retest the high currently being formed. The final phase of the 18.5-year cycle has turned parabolic, so I cannot completely rule this scenario out. However, since we are in the final 26-month, 4-year, and 9.25-year phases of the 18.5-year cycle, the greater probability is that we will see only a corrective rally with left translation, as the 26-month cycle turns bearish into 2026–2027. Therefore, the price target for the 26-month cycle trough is 37.64 +/– 3.97, and it should form between July 2025 and May 2026. Once the trough has formed, I would expect a 38.2% to 61.8% rally to the 26-month cycle crest two to five months later. I cannot provide a price target for this rally until the 26-month cycle trough has formed. From there, I would expect a two- or three-phased decline into the 18.5-year cycle trough at either 31.41 +/– 5.43 or a more severe decline toward 16.24 +/– 4.51 at any point over the next three years.

   981→## T-NOTES LINING UP FOR A 6-YEAR CYCLE CREST IN 2026
   982→
   983→by Gianni Di Poce, MMA Analyst T-Notes Cycles Start/Progress as of 1/1/26 Next Due 18-year October 2018, 8 years 2033–2039 6-year October 2023, 3 years 2028–2030 29-month October 2023, 27 months August 2025–October 2026 50-week January 2025, 51 weeks October 2025–April 2026
   984→
   985→## REVIEW
   986→
   987→T-Notes hit their lows of the year early in 2025, on January 13 at 107/06. This was a 50-week cycle low and set the stage for rising prices for the remainder of the year. The low was also significant because it confirmed the October 2023 low at 105/15.5 as the 6-year cycle bottom. As of this writing in November 2025, T-Notes are making new highs for the year above 114/00. However, prices have not taken out the 2024 high of 115/23.5 from September of that year. Thus, 2025 could turn out to be an “inside year” for T-Notes, in which the previous year’s high and low are not surpassed. The conclusion section of Forecast 2025 stated, “Our preferred outlook for 2025 is centered around a 6-year cycle trough being complete in October 2023. The 6-year cycle is still in its first 29-month phase, but since the greater 18-year cycle has turned bearish, there is a strong chance that the rally in T-Notes from the October 2023 low ends this year. Although T-Notes satisfied the upside target for 2024 in the 114/25–116/20 range by rallying as high as 115/23.5 on September 11, the duration of the rally was not long enough to qualify as a 6-year cycle crest. The sell-off that fol lowed from this September 11 crest is due to the 9–15 month cycle coming due, and it calls for a low no later than January 2025. This scenario would obviously be nullified if prices took out their low from October 2023 at 105/10.5… Assuming T-Notes are in a newer 6-year cycle from October 2023, another retest of the 114/25–116/20 range is in the cards for 2025. But it’ s also possible that high is exceeded, and that T-Notes could rally as high as 122/00–124/00 in that time band between April and October 2025. In fact, this upside target is supported by previous rallies in 6-year cycles. However, it’ s worth noting that most of the historical instances of rallies in 6-year cycles occurred during the secular bull market in T-Notes from 1982 to 2020. Thus, the historical cases may not prove to be as accurate as they once were, since T-Notes are in a long-term bear market now per the 18-year cycle turning bearish.” T-Notes still have not tested the 114/25–116/20 range, which is what I want to see before a 6-year cycle crest is complete. This means there could be higher prices or lower interest rates in 2026 before a continuation of the bearish 18-year cycle takes hold. The Federal Reserve also paused its rate cuts from December 2024 to September 2025. The central bank has resumed its rate cuts, and the market currently expects additional easing to continue well into 2026. This provides a macroeconomic backdrop for T-Notes to continue rallying, at least until inflationary pressures begin to increase again. Remember that rate cuts mean money printing,
   988→
   989→<!-- PAGE 131 END -->
   990→
   991→and, at some point, the return of inflation will coincide with another long-term cycle crest in T-Notes. Inflation typically leads to higher interest rates, and T-Note prices move inversely to interest rates. In other words, inflation is bearish for T-Notes.
   992→
   993→## THE 18-YEAR CYCLE
   994→
   995→2026 marks the eighth year of the 18-year cycle in T-Notes, measured from the October 2018 low at 117/13. This long-term cycle typically lasts 15–21 years, so we are not looking for a trough until 2033–2039, unless there is a case of cyclical contraction. This also implies that interest rates would continue to climb for the next 7–13 years at least. This is a bearish 18-year cycle because prices took out the low that began the cycle in October 2018. Additionally, the crest was formed in March 2020, which was only the second year of the cycle. When cycle crests occur in the first half of a cycle, the cycle is considered bearish. We expect the lowest price of the cycle to occur at its end. This bearish 18-year cycle continues to hang over the T-Note market and points to additional inflation problems until the long-term cycle bottoms.
   996→
   997→## THE 6-YEAR CYCLE
   998→
   999→The 18-year cycle breaks down into three 6-year cycles. The newer 6-year cycle scenario was confirmed in 2025, as prices never broke below the October 2023 low, and we are now beyond the 5- to 7-year orb from the October 2018 long-term cycle low. Thus, 2026 will begin the third year of the second 6-year cycle phase within the greater 18-year cycle, which is bearish. This 6-year cycle is the most important one for 2026 because the odds favor a 6-year cycle crest forming this year—especially if it did not already occur in September 2024. My bias is that the 6-year cycle crest is not complete yet, because the September 2024 high occurred only 11 months after the October 2023 low. Although a bearish 6-year cycle is expected overall, a bullish first phase of the cycle is still anticipated. More on this in the next section. Forecast 2025 stated, “Prices didn’t quite reach our upside objective for a 6-year cycle crest, which supports the idea that new highs could yet be on the horizon for 2025. Not to mention, the
  1000→
  1001→<!-- PAGE 132 END -->
  1002→
  1003→historical length of rallies for 6-year cycles in T-Notes has always lasted at least 18 months. This means that if October 2023 was truly the 6-year cycle trough, we wouldn’t look for the 6-year cycle crest before April 2025. Plus, the phase breakdown of the 6-year cycle suggests that there is still time left in this rally in T-Notes, assuming it is a newer 6-year cycle.” This supports the idea that a 6-year cycle crest will form in 2026. Remember that bearish cycles spend more time declining than advancing, so a 6-year cycle crest beyond 2026 would not align with a bearish 6-year cycle. The next 6-year cycle trough is not expected until 2028–2030, so the antici pated crest this year sets T-Notes up for another multi-year decline. New lows beneath the October 2023 low at 105/10.5 are also anticipated for this cycle’s bottom.
  1004→
  1005→## THE 29-MONTH CYCLE
  1006→
  1007→The 6-year cycle then breaks down into two or three 29-month cycles. The duration of the 6-year cycle determines whether there will be two or three 29-month cycle phases. Most 29-month cycles last between 22 and 36 months, and since January 2026 begins the 27th month from October 2023, T-Notes are already within the time band for a 29-month cycle trough. It is only the crest that still needs to be confirmed. Based on historical metrics, the 29-month cycle low is expected no later than October 2026. With the 6-year cycle bottom in October 2023, the 29-month cycle was reset as well. Forecast 2025 stated, “T-Notes are still in their first 29-month phase within the 6-year cycle, and as a rule, the first phase of every cycle is bullish. Historically, the majority of 29-month cycles have rallied for at least 9–27 months. The September 11, 2024, high would fall into this range for a 29-month cycle high, although it would be a bit early from a 6-year cycle standpoint, and, as a rule, the longer-term cycles overpower the shorter ones. Plus, given that the first phases are usually bullish, it would be prefer able to see it rally at least past the halfway mark of the cycle, say 15–16 months. This would call for a high as soon as January or February 2025, but, given the current technical picture of T-Notes, it is rather unrealistic. Thus, it would still be ideal for T-Notes to rally into April 2025 or beyond from a 29-month cycle standpoint.” T-Notes never hit a new 29-month cycle high in 2025, although prices are not far from exceeding the September 2024 crest at 115/23.5. There is still enough time in the 29-month cycle for new highs in 2026, although this supports the idea of a crest forming in the first half of the year. The 29-month cycle crest is lining up to coincide with the greater 6-year cycle crest. To narrow down the timeframe for a high even further, the 29-month cycle is broken down into two or three 50-week cycles that typically last 9–15 months. T-Notes began 2025 with a 50-week cycle trough on January 13, 2025, at 107/06. In theory, a 50-week cycle low could unfold before the start of 2026, but if not, then the cycle bottom would be expected no later than April 2026, as the beginning of the year corresponds to the 51st week, or 12th month, of this cycle. T-Notes are still in the second 50-week cycle phase within the greater 29-month cycle. In theory, a third phase could unfold in 2026 that aligns with the greater 29-month and 6-year cycle crests. This is a wild card for the cycle scenarios in T-Notes going into 2026.
  1008→
  1009→## GEOCOSMICS
  1010→
  1011→As of this writing in November 2025, the high for T-Notes occurred near several key outer-planetary aspects in April. However, there is still a chance that new highs could form before the calendar year ends. Forecast 2025 stated, “Looking ahead into 2025, the most notable observation to be had
  1012→
  1013→<!-- PAGE 133 END -->
  1014→
  1015→is a sign change of every outer planet within the year. Of course, Pluto will already be in Aquarius for good, but we’ll see Jupiter ingress into Cancer on June 9, Saturn ingress into Aries on May 24, Uranus ingress into Gemini on July 7, and Neptune ingress into Aries on March 30”. The analysis went on to state, “But it goes even further than these outer-planetary ingresses. Aside from the Jupiter–Saturn square and a square between Jupiter and Neptune on June 18, there are a few soft aspects between outer planets that could actually signal comfort, even if temporary, for the economy. Saturn is in sextile with Uranus on April 4 and August 11, while Uranus is in sextile with Neptune on August 28 and November 20. Interestingly, each of these sextile signatures occurs with the respective planets in different signs. The April 4 sextile between Saturn and Uranus will have Saturn in Pisces and Uranus in Taurus, while the August 11 sextile will have Saturn in Aries and Uranus in Gemini. The August 28 sextile between Uranus and Neptune has Uranus in Gemini and Neptune in Aries, but the November 20 sextile has Uranus in Taurus and Neptune in Pisces. This happens because of the retrograde motions that are going to take all of these outer planets back into their previous signs, except Jupiter and Pluto. Saturn retrogrades back into Pisces on September 1, Uranus retrogrades back into Taurus on November 7, and Neptune retrogrades back into Pisces on October 22.” It was actually near the sextile between Saturn and Uranus on April 4 that T-Notes completed their high of the year. There was also the Jupiter–Saturn square, whose central time band was in effect until June 2025. The second of three passages occurred on December 24, 2024, just a couple of weeks before the low of the year in T-Notes. It is not my view, however, that either of these highs or lows represented significant long-term cycle crests. The January 2025 low was, however, a 50-week trough. From an outer-planetary standpoint, 2026 is the sequel year to the initial ingresses that occurred in 2025. Pluto has already been in Aquarius, but 2026 will see Saturn definitively ingress into Aries for 2.5 years on February 13, Uranus definitively ingresses into Gemini for 7 years on April 25, and Neptune ingresses into Aries for 14 years on January 26. Interestingly, 2026 begins with another sextile between Saturn and Uranus on January 20. This is the same aspect that coincided with the 50-week bottom in January 2025. It cannot be ruled out that another 50-week cycle trough occurs in either January or February, but the primary geocosmic focus for 2026 surrounds the timing of a potential 6-year cycle crest in T-Notes. Based on the cycle counts discussed in the previous section, the timing for a 6-year cycle crest appears to favor the first or second quarter of 2026. It is worth noting that all of the outer-planetary ingresses will take place in the first half of 2026, including Jupiter’s ingress into Leo on June 30. Outer-planetary ingresses tend to correspond with larger psychological shifts among market partici pants, which aligns well with the prospect of a long-term cycle crest in T-Notes. There is also a sextile between Saturn and Pluto on March 28. Although sextiles are usually not the preferred aspect for marking long-term market reversals, this one could be especially important because of the Saturn–Pluto synodic cycle. Remember that the long-term bull market in bonds began roughly one year before the Saturn–Pluto conjunction of 1982 and then ended within two months of the Saturn–Pluto conjunction of January 2020. However, there are three outer-planetary aspects taking place in July 2026 that are shaping up to be very important for the bond market. The first is the Uranus–Pluto trine on July 18. Then, two days later, on July 20, there is an opposition between Jupiter and Pluto. That same day, there is also a trine between Jupiter and Neptune. The Uranus–Pluto trine will kick off the central time band of this signature, which will remain in effect until May 2028.
  1016→
  1017→<!-- PAGE 134 END -->
  1018→
  1019→The Uranus–Pluto synodic cycle is important for T-Notes as well, because the square signature between 2012 and 2015 coincided with “QE-3” from the Fed. Now that another signature is coming into effect, could the central bank initiate a new form of unconventional monetary policy? For this to occur, some sort of crisis in the bond market would likely need to play out, and, naturally, a long-term cycle crest would have to form. Uranus rules innovation, and Pluto rules debt. But both Jupiter and Neptune—planets that rule inflation—are involved here as well. Let’s not forget that Neptune in fire signs has historically been inflationary, too. The combination of the trine between Jupiter and Neptune and the opposition between Jupiter and Pluto increases the probability of a massive expansion in inflation expectations. This would be bearish for T-Notes and would lead to a rise in interest rates. But the wild card in this case is the Uranus–Pluto trine. Although it is not my bias that the Fed would intervene to stop a rise in interest rates this early in the 6-year cycle, at some point the central bank could step in with a surprising program—likely in the form of yield curve control—to stem the rise in interest rates. Uranus trine Pluto is the ideal aspect for such an intervention to occur, and it is my expectation that this will happen during the central time band between July 2026 and May 2028. It is not my view that it will occur in 2026, although it may be possible toward the end of the year if inflationary pressures get out of control too quickly. It is also important to tie in some transits to the Federal Reserve’s natal chart for clues in the T-Note market. The natal chart used for this analysis is set for December 23, 1913, at 6:02 p.m. in the Capitol Building in Washington, D.C. Forecast 2025 stated, “Note that the third and final Jupiter– Saturn square will hit the Fed’ s natal Pluto at zero degrees Cancer. Jupiter will be conjunct Pluto, while Saturn is square Pluto. Pluto is known as the “Four D Planet” (debts, downgrades, defaults, and deficits), and it rules debt, so it’ s obviously a very important planet for an entity that determines the price of that debt via interest rates. Jupiter conjunct Pluto could be one of two things. It could signal continued easing on behalf of the Fed, since Jupiter has an affinity towards growth, but it could also mean an oversupply of debt. In this scenario, the Fed may actually have to slow down on interest rate cuts.” Interestingly, the Fed did pause in its rate cuts, but it occurred after the second Jupiter–Saturn square rather than the final one in June 2025, when Jupiter was on the Fed’s natal Pluto. The Fed then resumed rate cuts with Jupiter near its ascendant in September 2025. Due to Jupiter’s retrograde, two more conjunctions will take place to the Fed’s ascendant in Cancer: the first on January 25, 2026, and the second on April 24, 2026. My view is that rate cuts will continue beyond April 24, at least into Jupiter’s opposition to the Fed’s natal Uranus at 5 degrees Aquarius. This will occur after Jupiter ingresses into Leo, and it will unfold around the same time that transiting Pluto comes within orb of a conjunction to the Fed’s natal Uranus. This combination of planetary aspects seems to be setting up a showdown over control of the Fed. The natal Uranus in Aquarius represents the central bank’s strong sense of independence, and it looks to be coming under a rather dramatic (Jupiter) attempt at coercion (Pluto) beginning in the second half of 2026. It is worth noting that Jerome Powell’s term as Fed Chair is set to end in May 2026 as well, although he is scheduled to stay on as a governor until 2028.
  1020→
  1021→<!-- PAGE 135 END -->
  1022→
  1023→This geocosmic setup may also involve Scott Bessent’s natal Saturn at six degrees of Aquarius (born August 21, 1962; birth time unknown), which is conjunct the Federal Reserve’s natal Uranus. Combined with transiting Pluto conjunct the Fed’s natal Uranus, this suggests that the Treasury Secretary could begin to have a major influence on the Fed’s policy decisions. There have already been rumors of Bessent being appointed Fed Chair, but the current law prohibits one person from holding both positions at the same time. Regardless, the central bank’s independence appears to be under real threat in 2026—and it does not end with these aspects, either. The conjunction between Saturn and Neptune on February 20, 2026, at zero degrees Aries will be conjunct the central bank’s midheaven and square its Sun. This spells an identity crisis and raises questions surrounding its authority. Authoritative deception is in play here, potentially arising from faulty data being sent its way, which could undermine its policy decisions. This already happened in 2025, when more than 900,000 jobs magically disappeared, and the Fed realized it was behind the curve on cutting rates. Something similar could occur in 2026, but perhaps involving understated inflation data that encourages the central bank to continue cutting rates.
  1024→
  1025→## CONCLUSION
  1026→
  1027→T-Notes are shaping up for additional upside in 2026 now that the newer 6-year cycle scenario from October 2023 has been confirmed. My preferred outlook is for prices to rally into a 6-year cycle crest in the 121/00–123/00 range sometime between April and August 2026. Keep in mind that this will coincide with a 29-month cycle crest as well. The big question is whether another 50-week cycle will begin before the 29-month cycle tops out, as there can be two or three 50-week cycles within a 29-month cycle, depending on the cycle’s length. The highs from 2025, 2024, and 2023 are expected to be exceeded in 2026. Since a 29-month cycle trough is due by October, the 6-year cycle crest is not likely to produce an immediate sharp pullback. This means that at some point, there will be a strong, tradable bounce in T-Notes in 2026. However, a significant secondary lower high beneath the high of the year is a potential scenario in the fourth quarter of 2026. The geocosmics that begin in 2026—especially the Uranus–Pluto trine—point to a managedstyle decline in the T-Note prices over the coming years. Keep in mind that the time band for a 6-year cycle trough begins in 2028 and that the central time band of the Uranus–Pluto trine lasts into May 2028. Since the greater 18-year cycle is bearish, we expect the 6-year cycle phase to record its lowest price at the end of its cycle. This means a drop to 105/00–105/10 should be in order, but that is not in the cards for 2026, unless we see an expanded 5- to 7-year cycle that takes prices to new lows. This is not our bias, however. Instead, my preferred scenario is to see T-Notes form a 50-week cycle crest in the 114/25–116/20 range sometime in January or February, followed by a 50-week cycle trough in February or March. Then prices would commence another rally into a 29-month and 6-year crest by August. The target is as high as 121/00–123/00. A drop into a 29-month cycle low could then occur, with prices falling back into the 114/25–116/20 zone. After that, another rally can occur into year-end, but it will not take out the 6-year cycle crest. My expectation is for the 29-month cycle that follows the current one to be bearish.
  1028→
  1029→<!-- PAGE 136 END -->
  1030→
  1031→The threat against the Fed’s independence may not actually work out as intended. In theory, the attempted takeover may begin very late in 2026, after rising rates and inflation start to become a problem again. The objective appears to be to artificially peg interest rates below the prevailing rate of inflation in order to devalue the debt. Structural issues in the bond market could easily continue into the mid-2030s, which lines up with an 18-year cycle bottom. There will also be an opposition between Saturn and Pluto around that time, and Neptune will be in the later degrees of Aries. All in all, this is a bond market that continues to price in default risk and inflation risk—mainly from gov ernments versus private corporations, which may actually prove to offer a safer haven compared with government bonds going forward.

  1061→## CURRENCY MARKETS IN 2026
  1062→
  1063→Currency markets were very active in 2025. The U.S. Dollar was weak, while the star performer was the Swiss Franc. Everyone wanted the safety of the neutral Swiss Franc, even though its central bank cut its interest rate to 0% to stop its appreciation. A lower dollar benefits international trade for U.S. corporations, which is also a reason why the Swiss central bank didn’t want its currency to appreciate so much.   1097→## THE U.S. DOLLAR INDEX (DXY)
  1098→
  1099→by Ulric Aspegren, MMA Analyst
  1100→
  1101→## REVIEW
  1102→
  1103→In mid-November 2024, when the previous yearly U.S. Dollar report was completed, the green back was rising from the September 27, 2024, low at 100.15 USD (9). Last year’s Forecast 2025 book detailed: “The hard nut to crack question is: did the greater cycle that started in 2008 (4) end in 2021(8) after 12.8 years, or are we 16.6 years into an older 16-year greater cycle that also originated in 2008? The former could set up a long-term bullish run for the U.S. Dollar Index, while the latter would be very bearish for the greenback, as the 16-year cycle would be ripe to head lower into its greater cycle abyss.” Looking back on the last twelve months, the Dollar succeeded in ascending a respectable 10% from the September 2024 low (9) to 110.17 on January 13, 2025 (I), but then ran completely out of steam. So far, a total descent of 12.7% for nine long months has followed, resulting in a low on September 17 at 96.21 (10). The greenback has managed to regain 4.30%, reaching 100.36 on November 5. Could the September 2025 low have been the long-term cycle bottom for the U.S. Dollar Index, or is there more bearishness to come? The DXY closed on November 14, 2025, at 99.299 USD. Preferred Cycle (Start) Progress Next event 16-year (Mar 2008) 5.2-year (Jan 2021) 36-month (Jul 2023) 14-month (Sep 2024) 17.6 years 4.9 years 28 months 13.5 months Combined narrowed down long-term cycle trough expected
  1104→
  1105→## January–June 2026.
  1106→
  1107→## THE LONG-TERM CYCLES IN THE U.S. DOLLAR INDEX
  1108→
  1109→As of this writing in mid-November 2025, it is still a challenge to etch out the long-term outlook. We got a greater cycle start at the 2008 low (4), at 70.70. If this cycle is still operational, then we are 17.6 years into it and heading south towards its greater cycle bottom. Historically, this is clearly longer than the two previous 13.9- and 15.5-year cycles, which could mean that the Dollar is instead 4 years and change into a new, greater cycle that commenced in January 2021, at 89.20 (8). If this is true, then the greenback is on a long-term bullish path, on the way towards a greater cycle crest, expected in about three years’ time. However, as we only have two samples to compare with, we just cannot forge a reliable long-term outlook with such a small sample size. We have to search elsewhere for clues.
  1110→
  1111→## THE POLITICAL CYCLE IN THE U.S. DOLLAR
  1112→
  1113→The previous Forecast 2025 book stated: “Under a Democrat administration, the Dollar tends to rally into the 16-year cycle crest. Under a Republican, it tends to fall into the 16-year cycle low. Hence, the political cycle in the U.S. Dollar does not correspond with a greater cycle trough in 2021 (8), as the Democrats were in the White House. However, the political cycle does align with a 16-year greater cycle crest established in 2022 (H), since the Democrats were still in control of the presi dency. Now that the Republicans have overtaken the Oval Office, it would indicate, according to the political cycle, that the U.S. Dollar Index is heading towards a 16-year cycle trough. My preferred outlook is therefore bearish.”
  1114→
  1115→<!-- PAGE 139 END -->
  1116→
  1117→## THE 5.2-YEAR LONG-TERM CYCLE IN THE U.S. DOLLAR
  1118→
  1119→The 16-year cycle splits in the bearish long-term scenario into three 5.2-year cycles. The prices are here 4.8 years into the third 5.2-year cycle, which started on January 6, 2021, at 89.20 (8). Both the final 5.2-year and the 16-year cycle crests were established together on September 28, 2022, at 114.78 (H). Time-wise, the future 5.2-year cycle low, which should coincide with the 16-year cycle trough, is projected to unfold sometime between March 2025 and March 2027 with its one-year orb. Hence, we are now within the bottoming time frame for the long-term cycle trough. As the expectation is that this final 5.2-year cycle should be bearish, we will use its historical bearish price declines to estimate the price target for its forthcoming long-term cycle low. The historical bearish descents from the previous 5.2-year cycle crests are between 25–48% (using 75% of the cases), producing a price target span of 60–87 USD. We will use this span as the overall price target range for the 16-year cycle trough. Consequently, the September 17, 2025, low, at 96.21 (10), appears to be too shallow for a greater cycle low. Hence, my bias is that the greenback will continue lower. U.S. DOLLAR INDEX Preferred Monthly Chart, as of November 14, 2025

  1121→## THE 36-MONTH LONG-TERM CYCLE IN THE U.S. DOLLAR
  1122→
  1123→The 5.2-year cycle breaks down most of the time into two 36-month cycles. We are now 28 months into the second 36-month cycle that started on July 14, 2023, at 99.58 (9). The crest of the current 36-month cycle did occur on January 30, 2025, at 110.17 (I). This second 36-month cycle, with its 6-month orb, is due to bottom out sometime between January 2026 and January 2027. As this final 36-month cycle is anticipated to end simultaneously with the completion of the current 5.2-year cycle, we can, via overlapping, concentrate the timing for the forthcoming 16-year cycle trough, to January 2026–January 2027 as well. Historically, prices have dropped 19–23% when the 36-month cycles have been bearish. We can therefore estimate the price target range for the upcoming bearish 36-month cycle low to 84–89 USD. Hence, by overlapping with the overall price target for the 16-year cycle low, we obtain an 84–87 USD span as one price area where the upcoming long-term cycle low could occur.

  1129→## THE 14-MONTH INTERMEDIATE-TERM CYCLE IN THE U.S. DOLLAR INDEX
  1130→
  1131→The 36-month long-term cycle can be split into either three 45-week (10-month) cycles or two 14-month cycles, or a combination of both. The best fit at this time is that the first 14-month intermediate-term cycle was completed on September 27, 2024, at 100.15, as it was 14 months away from the July 2023 low. The current 36-month cycle should thus be in its second and final 14-month cycle. Last year’s report stated: “As we are in a bearish long-term scenario, the expectation is that this second 14-month cycle should peak out 1.4 to 3.7 months after the September 2024 low. The bearish historical crest data generate a time target range of November 8, 2024–January 17, 2025, for the forthcoming 14-month cycle top. Price-wise, again using the bearish crest data, we obtain a price target range of 104.62–110.24, which represents a 4.5–10% rise.” The bearish 14-month cycle crest was established on January 13, 2025, at 110.17, which was both within the forecasted time and price target spans. My preferred view is that we are 13.5 months into the second 14-month cycle. As the Dollar is assumed to be in a bearish long-term scenario, the forecast is that prices should now decline into the second 14-month cycle low, projected to occur with its 5.5-month orb, sometime between June 2025 and April 2026. This 14-month cycle bottom is also anticipated to be a 16-year cycle trough, which narrows the time target to January 2026–January 2027. Hence, via additional overlapping, we can further concentrate the timing for the 16-year cycle bottom to January 2026–April 2026. This is a very tight time gap for a 16-year cycle trough. Hence, let’s not forget that the greater cycle is always in command, and the long-term cycle low could, at least potentially, come in at the latest, by March 2027. A bearish 14-month cycle low is expected historically to come in at a descent of 10%–22%, which computes to 86–99 USD. As a 16-year cycle trough is due to unfold, this decline might be too shallow. Nevertheless, we have already estimated a first price target range of 84–87 USD, so we can overlap with the 14-month cycle low price objective to further narrow down our target to 86–87 USD. When the long-term cycle trough is behind us, the prices should rise to a bullish 14-month cycle crest, expected to top out six to eleven months after the low and at an increase of 13–23%.

  1139→## TECHNICALS

  1143→## BIAS
  1144→
  1145→Last year, even though the prices were rising from the September 2024 low (9), my bias was bearish for the Dollar, a judgment that was only hanging in the balance on the political cycle. It was within its time target span, but as it was not within the estimated price target range, I am biased that the greenback is heading lower and thus that the 16-year cycle trough is still ahead. Nevertheless, if, against my bias, the prices would now instead rise, overtaking, at first, the lower parallel line, then the Dollar could be in a long-term bullish trend from a greater cycle trough, cemented in January 2021, or even in September 2025. This bullish outlook would be powerfully reinforced if the previous 14-month cycle crest, established on January 13, 2025, at 110.17 (I), is surpassed, as it would confirm that a new 14-month cycle is in a bullish trend. However, it is only when the September 2022 crest, at 114.78 (H), is overtaken that we would have the confirmation that the long-term bullish alternative is active.

  1149→## U.S. DOLLAR/YEN
  1150→
  1151→by Gianni Di Poce, MMA Analyst
  1152→
  1153→## REVIEW
  1154→
  1155→The Dollar/Yen had an inside year in 2025. The high of the year occurred early in the year, on January 10 at 158.87, while the low of the year occurred on April 22, 2025, at 139.86. This was below the high of 2024 but above the low of 2024 as well. Throughout most of the year, the Bank of Japan (BOJ) allowed interest rates on Japanese government bonds (JGBs) to rise. This caused some weakness in the Dollar/Yen exchange rate, but with the election of Sanae Takaichi in 2025, markets are starting to price in a return to “Abenomics” policies. These economic policies centered on weakening the Japanese Yen in order to manage the country’s debt load. This creates a backdrop for potential strength in the Dollar/Yen in 2025, and it is supported by the long-term cycle situation as well. Last year’s Conclusion section stated, “The weight of the evidence of the Dollar/Yen being in a new 4.125-year cycle is very compelling. The biggest question for the Dollar/Yen now, given its lateness of the 16.5-year cycle, is whether it can go on to make new cycle and multi-decade highs. Given the geocosmic backdrop, our bias is that USD/JPY will retest the 164.00 +/- 2.00 zone and probably rally as high as 175.00–177.00. It cannot entirely be ruled out that a 16.5-year cycle crest forms in 2025 in this zone of 175.00–177.00, but this is not our bias. On the contrary, the geocosmics of 2025 suggest we’re only getting a preview, due to retrograde motions, of a more profound crisis to come in the Dollar/Yen in 2026. Eventually, we could see the Dollar/Yen rally as high as 220.00–225.00, but probably not in 2025. This may coincide with the greater long-term 16.5-year cycle.” While the Dollar/Yen did not rally up to the target of 175.00–177.00, it held firmly in the 139.00 +/– 2.00 zone, essentially completing a double bottom to the September 2024 low. This low occurred seven months later, and it is not uncommon to see retests of important long-term cycle bottoms 6–22 months later. It will also be a matter of whether the Bank of Japan reverts to a more accommodative monetary policy and stops allowing yields on JGBs to rise. There may be a final attempt at lowering yields with the new administration in power.
  1156→
  1157→## THE LONG-TERM CYCLES IN THE DOLLAR/YEN
  1158→
  1159→The longest cycle to watch in the Dollar/Yen is 16.5 years. The prior low was on October 31, 2011, at 75.55, and 2026 starts the 15th year of the cycle. This long-term cycle points to a low around August 2028 +/– 3.5 years, so a low is due at any time. But first, the crest for this long-term cycle must be confirmed. As it stands, the crest from July 2024 at 161.99 is holding, but there is still a possibility that USD/JPY can rally one final time before reversing lower. Historically, the 16.5-year cycle broke down into phases lasting 5.5 years, or 55–77 months. However, in this cycle, a two-phase pattern composed of two 8.25-year cycles appears to have taken hold. An 8.25-year cycle trough unfolded in March 2020, making 2026 the sixth year in the 8.25-year cycle. This cycle is calling for a low between 2027 and 2029, so in theory, USD/JPY could still hit a new cycle high this year before beginning a drop into an 8.25-year cycle low. This 8.25-year cycle crest would form together with the 16.5-year cycle crest.

  1165→## THE INTERMEDIATE-TERM CYCLES IN THE DOLLAR/YEN
  1166→
  1167→The 4.125-year cycle breaks down further into either two 22.5-month cycle phases or three 17-month cycle phases. The 22.5-month cycle represents not only a half-cycle phase of the 4.125year cycle, but also one of the three phases of the 5.5-year cycle. The 4.125-year cycle that bottomed in September 2024 broke down into a three-phase pattern of 17-month phases. Forecast 2025 stated, “The question now is whether this final 4.125-year cycle phase to the greater 8.25-year cycle will break down into two 22.5-month or three 17-month cycles. It is still too early to tell, but January 2025 will begin the 4th month in this new intermediate-term cycle. Since it’ s the first phase of a new 4.125year cycle, we anticipate it to be bullish and rally into June or July at least.” So far, the high of this first phase of the 4.125-year cycle occurred on January 10, 2025, at 158.87. Thus, my expectation is for new cycle highs to follow in 2026, although it is not yet certain what the phase breakdown of this cycle will be. January 2026 will start the 16th month from the September 2024 low, and so if there is going to be a 17-month cycle phase, then a crest could be anticipated in the first quarter of 2026 at the latest. A low would be expected no later than April or May 2026. However, if there are going to be two 22.5-month cycle phases, USD/JPY could easily rally into the back half of 2026. A 22.5-month cycle trough would be due by December 2026, though. Even so, the intermediate-term cycles point to more upside for USD/JPY throughout the majority of 2026.

  1373→## THE 12-YEAR CYCLE IN CRUDE OIL AND ITS PHASES
  1374→
  1375→The long-term cyclical analysis in Crude Oil begins with a potential 36-year cycle. The exact periodicity of this cycle is unknown because there haven’t been enough occurrences in Crude Oil to quantify it to a high degree of statistical probability. The previous 36-year cycle was from April 1986 until April 2020, which was 34 years. The 36-year cycle can be subdivided into either two 18-year cycles with a range of 15–21 years, or three 12-year cycles with a range of 10–14 years. Historical analysis suggests that the 12-year cycle is more prominent. From the low of April 1986, the next 12-year trough was February of 1999, which was 12 years and 10 months. Following that, the next trough was January of 2009, which was 9 years and 11 months. The final 12-year cycle was April 2020, which was 11 years and 3 months later. This means that the next 12-year cycle trough is due 2032 +/– 2 years. As shown in the chart above, the 12-year cycle has a tendency to break down into three 4-year or 44-month cyclical phases, with a range of 36–52 months. Therefore, my preferred outlook is that the current 44-month cycle formed on May 4, 2023, at 63.64. The trough formed under the 22-month MA and even tested the 72-month MA. The next 44-month cyclical trough is due Janu ary 2027 +/– 8 months. In January 2026, we will be commencing the 32nd month of the current 44-month cycle, which has turned bearish by taking out the low that commenced the cycle in April of 2025. There is also a chance that the current 12-year cycle is breaking down into a two-phased cycle of 6 years (range of 5–7 years). This would mean that the 6-year cycle is due between 2025–2027, preferably with Saturn in Pisces and in orb of the Saturn–Neptune conjunction. This is my alternative outlook, but it deserves attention because a case can be made that a 6-year half cycle is breaking down further into two 3-year half-cycle phases with a range of 30–42 month, similar to the U.S. stock market cycle.

Whilst we are yet to see the full infla tionary impact of Trump’s trade wars, it is also worth noting that Crude Oil is one of the key com modities responsible for inflation. The last time Neptune went over the vernal axis was 1861, which corresponds to the highest value in WTI (when adjusted for inflation) during the American Civil War. Crude Oil tends to form important reversals in close proximity to the retrograde motion of Neptune and Jupiter. Neptune will go retrograde on July 7, 2026, until December 12, 2026. Jupiter will go retrograde on November 11, 2025, and will be retrograde until March 10, 2026. It will start its next retrograde from December 12, 2026 (same day as Neptune) until April 12, 2027.
  1392→
  1393→## CONCLUSION
  1394→
  1395→Whilst the geocosmic outlook is tense, the cycle studies take precedence and remain bearish. The cycle studies dictate a bearish move down into the preferred 44-month trough (May 2026–September 2027) or the alternative outlook of the 6-year trough (April 2025–April 2027). In the latter case, a three-year cycle would be due November 2025–November 2026. This overlap zone could be the hot
  1396→
  1397→<!-- PAGE 164 END -->
  1398→
  1399→zone. The price action will help guide us as to which cycle is forming, since the price target for the 44-month trough is 51.01 +/– 5.20, whilst the target for the 6-year trough may be the steeper decline to 28.17 +/– 7.89. If the geopolitics flare up before either of these two troughs has formed, we are only going to see a corrective rally, which will be followed by a sharp move back down, as seen in 2025. However, if geopolitics is aligned with either the 44-month or 6-year low, we are likely to see a spectacular rally that has a good chance of recording a new ATH. I would expect this low to be accompanied by bullish oscillator divergence in the CCI of the weekly chart. Confirmation for the rally will be a weekly or monthly close above the descending trend lines shown in my charts.
